News.title: Boy, 14, ‘who had sex with teacher 30 times’ denies being ‘fantasist’ & claims she paraded around school in mini skirt
News.content:
'SEX SHAME' Boy, 14, ‘who had sex with teacher 30 times’ denies being ‘fantasist’ & claims she paraded around school in mini skirt

A TEEN who allegedly sex with his teacher up to 30 times denied he is a “fantasist” – and accused her of parading around school in a mini skirt.

Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, is accused of abusing two boys at Christ’s College in Finchley, North London when they were aged 14 and 15 in the 1980s.



The teacher – then aged 25 – allegedly “engaged in flirtatious conduct” with the pupils and “engaged in sexual relationships with them both”.

Giving evidence at Harrow Crown Court, the 14-year-old told jurors he slept with Bowen “about 20 or 30 times”.



He also denied being a “fantasist” who invented the allegations – branding the suggestion “quite insulting”.

The boy claimed some of the sexual acts Bowen asked him to perform were “perverse”, adding: “I’m a ‘fantasist’, right?

“That’s not a part of anyone’s ­fantasy, to be involved in perversion.”

In a police interview, the boy said Bowen would dress in a “sexually provocative” way while teaching chemistry at the all-boys’ school.

He described her outfits as “tight Levi’s jeans and black skinny pants that you could see everything in, and a black mini skirt”.

The boy also told police how on one occasion, the boys were looking at a porn magazine when Bowen took it from them.



Jurors heard he expected her to confiscate but she instead “pointed to an image of a naked woman” and said “that’s what my p***y looks like”.

Jurors heard Bowen went on to have sex with the first boy between 20 and 30 times and he believed they were in a relationship.

The court heard the boy’s mum later became suspicious and called Bowen, who denied anything was happening.



When the alleged relationship continued after the holidays, his mum called the school and was told Bowen was no longer working there with “no reason or explanation given”.

Bowen later told the boy she was leaving the UK to stay at a kibbutz in Israel, the court heard.

The boy first disclosed the alleged abuse to a partner, who told him to go to police.

When Bowen was interviewed in 2015, she claimed he was a “bit of a nuisance” and “besotted” with her.

Jurors heard she described the sexual relationship claims as “just pure fantasy”.



As a result of the allegations, Bowen faced a Teaching Regulation Authority hearing in 2022.

The teacher is also accused of letting the second boy touch her breasts and kiss her during lunch at a cafe near the school.

The court heard he later read about the TRA hearing online and came forward after encouragement from his wife and family.



He claimed he was “goaded” by other boys at the school into kissing “young and attractive” Bowen.

The pupil also remembered touching her breasts and putting his hand near her crotch – to which “she would not react negatively”, it was said.

Prosecutor Madeleine Wolfe said: “The prosecution case is that when Ms Bowen worked at the school, that she engaged in flirtatious conduct towards these two boys and she encouraged and engaged in sexual relationships with them both and they were 14 to 15-years-old.

“The sexual abuse was notably worse to the first pupil who she engaged in acts of sexual intercourse. With the second pupil the abuse was limited to inappropriate kissing.

“The prosecution do not suggest Ms Bowen forced herself on either boy. Viewed superficially, these boys may have appeared willing to engage in flirtatious and sexual activity.



“But the prosecution remind you she was a teacher in a position of trust and authority. By flirting with them and engaging in sexual activity with them she exploited her position for her own sexual gratification.

“As these boys were exploited in that way, any apparent agreement on their part was not genuine consent to the sexual activity. She denied any form of sexual activity, whether that’s kissing or sexual intercourse with either.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bowen denies eight counts of indecent assault.

The trial continues.

News.title: Parents have custody of baby born against their wishes after surrogate defied order to abort pregnancy over heart defect
News.content:
SURROGACY DRAMA Parents have custody of baby born against their wishes after surrogate defied order to abort pregnancy over heart defect

A BABY born to a surrogate mother in Texas is now in the custody of his biological parents after they demanded an abortion over a heart defect.

McKenna West, a nurse from Alaska, gave birth to a boy, who she named Gabriel, on Wednesday – despite urgent pleas from his parents that she terminate the pregnancy after the diagnosis.



Nausheen Gilkar, 43, and Omar Ahmed, 45, were given the newborn while he receives medical care.

Lawyer for the couple, Lee Bunder, said his clients were placing the child’s health first and following the advice of doctors.



He also told TMZ: “As if the heartbreak of his condition were not enough, they are devastated to see their family tragedy transformed into political theatre by the Texas Attorney General’s office and McKenna West.”

The surrogate refused to end the pregnancy after being told that a series of operations could give the baby a chance at life.

The child was diagnosed with the rare birth defect – which means that the left side of his heart is too small and cannot pump blood to the rest of his body – during her 20-week ultrasound.

West said earlier scans and genetic tests had appeared normal, adding it was “completely unexpected.”

After the devastating news, Gilkar and Ahmed told her to get an abortion – but she refused.

The contract between the biological parents and West had a clause that allowed termination if there was an “anomaly” during the pregnancy.



Instead, she relocated to Texas after finding a hospital in Dallas that has a high success rate for babies with the defect.

Her lawyer, Lincoln Wilson, confirmed that his client is readying for a court battle to become the legal parent of Gabriel – and likened the contract to a “hitman contract.”

He told the New York Post: “These forced abortion clauses that demand that women have to be required to abort a child at the late term are quite common in surrogacy contracts.



“There’s some contracts the law doesn’t enforce. Like the law doesn’t enforce a hitman contract.

“This is basically a hitman contract, and we think that even if you accept a liberal view of abortion rights, the right to get an abortion also entails the right to not get an abortion.”

Wilson further added that West is seeking parentage of the child because she gave birth in Texas.

“In Texas, if you give birth to a child, it’s your child,” he added, threatening to take the case up to the US Supreme Court if necessary.

His client currently has no legal authority over the newborn because of a temporary restraining order filed by Gilkar and Ahmed.



This also means that she cannot make any decisions about his care, including on medical decisions, and bars her from representing herself as a parent, it was reported.

The baby will soon undergo a series of heart surgeries, the first of which is called the Norwood procedure.

It is followed by the Glenn procedure at around four to six months and the Fontan operation at roughly two or three years old.

NewYork-Presbyterian says around 72 percent of children receiving surgical treatment survive to age five.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Among those who reach five, approximately 90 percent survive to 18, although patients require lifelong heart care and may later need further procedures or a transplant.



Court documents reportedly describe the baby as a standard-risk patient whose condition may be an isolated heart defect.

News.title: Nine Brits & babies in prams among 36 rescued by choppers after getting lost in Alps and walking INCHES from cliff edge
News.content:
ALPS AIRLIFT Nine Brits & babies in prams among 36 rescued by choppers after getting lost in Alps and walking INCHES from cliff edge

NINE Brits – including babies in prams – were dramatically airlifted from a mountainside in the Alps after getting lost on a treacherous hiking trail.

Mountain rescue teams were scrambled after the group strayed onto a precarious route close to a sheer cliff edge.



Alpine crews were called at around 5.15pm on Sunday after reports that up to 15 people were lost.

They had been hiking down from the Wildspitz chairlift mountain station in Sölden, Austria, intending to make their way back to the nearby Ötztal valley.



But the group took a wrong turn and quickly found themselves in danger.

Minutes later, another distress call came in reporting that more people were lost in the area, including an injured amateur hiker.

Multiple helicopters were scrambled to search the mountainside, where rescuers eventually found 36 people wandering through the wilderness.

The group was made up of three separate families – including 17 Belgians, nine Brits, seven Austrians and three Americans.

Among them were two babies in prams, with their parents pushing them along a path described by rescuers as “completely unsuitable for strollers”.

Rescue operation boss Jakob Fiegl told Kronen Zeitung that some members of the group “were barely half a meter from the abyss and could hardly keep their feet standing”.



“There was even a stroller in the area where falls were imminent,” he added.

The group was found at an elevation of around 7,500ft, but had become scattered across the mountainside by the time the helicopters arrived.

“In some cases, they were separated by as much as 200 metres in altitude,” Fiegl said.

Helicopters initially carried 14 people to safety, with several needing to be winched aboard by rope.

Rescuer Stephan Kuen said he had to carry out a dramatic rescue of two boys trapped in a steep gully.



“I built a belay station and then secured one of the boys, who was dangerously close to a rock slab,” he said.

“Then I rappelled us down to the boy’s brother, from where we were airlifted out.”

The boys’ father watched the high-stakes rescue from higher up the mountain, where he was with other family members.

They were all airlifted to safety.

Meanwhile, rescuers escorted the remaining 22 people down the mountain on foot or in emergency road vehicles.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fiegl said the operation had been extremely perilous.

“This story could have ended very differently; their rescue was touch and go,” he said.

News.title: What REALLY happened when Ryanair passenger’s head was sucked from cabin window in mid-air as bombshell probe released
News.content:
A RYANAIR passenger was partially sucked out of plane at 16,000ft after broken engine parts shattered his window, a probe has confirmed.

Ljubiša Karovic, 63, was left on the “brink of death” before his wife and other brave passengers managed to pull him back into the cabin.



The Serbian businessman was left with “serious injuries” after his head and neck were exposed to brutal 370mph winds on the flight from Thessaloniki, Greece, to Memmingen, Germany.

The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) wrote in a preliminary report that there was an “engine fan-blade-out (FBO) failure” shortly after take-off.



The Boeing 737 jet, operated by subsidiary Malta Air, climbed to 16,000ft before the pilots received a “high vibration” alert from the right engine.

The NTSB report said: “They reduced the engine power and initiated the ‘Engine High Vibration non-normal checklist’.

“Shortly after, the engine vibration indication was reduced. The crew subsequently continued the climb on autopilot.”

But the engine fires then increased dramatically before the crew heard a loud bang and the cabin altitude warning began to sound.



The flight crew then declared an emergency, donned their oxygen masks and began an immediate descent.

Ljubiša had been asleep in seat 11F when he was pulled from his seat nine minutes and 30 seconds after take-off.

His wife, Svetlana Grković, clung onto his legs for around five minutes before others helped pull Ljubiša back inside and move him to row 12.



Passengers then tried jamming the open window with luggage, before someone “retrieved a metal box to bring back to row 11”.

A doctor who was a passenger on the plane looked after Ljubiša until the flight returned to Thessaloniki.

Describing the horror ordeal to Bild, he said: “I fell asleep… After some time I got woken up by a massive bang like a bomb. Only for one moment I was conscious and cannot remember the rest.

“I had blood all over me, blood was dripping from my face and my hands.

“As soon as I close my eyes, images appear of the nightmare I experienced. Those few minutes, it is simply a nightmare, which I cannot explain with words.



“I am not even contemplating getting on another flight. Every time I hear an airplane, I get stress and a fever. I am not well at all when I hear an airplane.”

The NTSB report noted that the engine had gone ultrasonic inspections in May this year with no finding of fault.

Investigators suggested the break could have been caused by a bird strike as “bird remains, including feathers, were recovered” from the engine.

Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary previously said initial findings suggest that “foreign object damage” caused the incident rather than age or servicing conditions of the aircraft.

In 2018, a passenger was killed in a similar incident on a Southwest Airlines 737 flight from New York LaGuardia to Dallas Love Field.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

An elderly passenger was partially sucked out and had to be pulled back inside by heroic passengers and crew after the aircraft was pierced by shrapnel at 32,000ft.

Mum-of-two and banking executive Jennifer Riordan suffered fatal head injuries.

News.title: Beating Binface was the easy part – now Farage faces the real challenge to fix Reform’s cracks & take fight to Burnham
News.content:
SPEAK to Nigel Farage and he will insist that this by-election campaign has been worth it.

Other parties dismissing it as a “gimmick” shows their contempt for the voters, he says.



And now finally the Reform leader thinks he has a bulletproof answer to all those questions about the £5million donation.

“You are not my judge: The people of Clacton are my judge, and they have just given me a stonking vote of confidence”.



Maybe there is something in that.

But Mr Farage should be alarmed that, while he has been busy at the Essex seaside, Andy Burnham has leapfrogged him in the polls.

Having led for 15 months, Reform has now suffered a slump at the hands of the new PM.

He is banking on this fizzling out in a matter of months, but there are still certainly some cracks starting to show in Reform.



Internal tensions are starting to break into the open, and holes are being picked in flagship policies.

The Standards Commissioner is also likely to resume his probe into the £5million donation.

Mr Farage is clearly a formidable campaigner and reader of the public mood.

But Clacton was the easy part. Now come the hard yards to convince swing voters.

Mr Farage triggered the by-election amid an ongoing row into his finances including a £5million gift he failed to declare.



He hoovered up a decisive 22,239 to Count Binface’s 9,455, equalling a 12,784 majority.

Ahead of the official result this morning, Mr Farage claimed an “overwhelming victory” to his supporters that dwarfed his 8,405 majority in 2024.

He said: “In doing so, we have beaten the candidate for the uniparty: Count Binface.”

But he told activists he would not be attending the count at the town hall and alleged that agitators were planning to disrupt it.

He said: “I am damned if I am going to stand on a stage, having won a resounding victory, and be demeaned and humiliated by nobodies.



“I will not, sadly, be attending the count.”

A Reform spokesman added: “Essex Police advised Nigel not to attend the count tonight due to a credible threat against him.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yet the force appeared to dispute the claims, saying: “We have a proportionate and robust policing operation to ensure the safety and security of all participants in the count.”

Instead the Reform leader addressed cheering crowds of grassroots members at so-called “Farage Fest” in Clacton.

News.title: Monster wildfire leaves houses in ruin as families reveal ‘ash raining from the sky’ as they grabbed bags & fled homes
News.content:
AN “APOCALYPTIC” wildfire has left homes in ruins as families reveal ash was “raining from the sky” as they grabbed their bags and fled.

PM Andy Burnham has praised firefighters working in “incredibly difficult conditions” yesterday in Stourbridge, as well as other blazes across the West Midlands fuelled by extreme heat and high winds.



Local resident Jane Baxter said she could “see the flames from our bedroom window” and described the “horrendous…choking smell in the air”.

She and neighbours were given a few minutes to gather their belongings and she eventually fled with the blaze just 200 yards away.



The wildfire raged out of control yesterday afternoon, starting as a massive grass fire ignited near Stourbridge Golf Club around 1.30pm.

Stourbridge local Steff Jones told Sky News the smoke was “very, very strong”, adding that “ash has been raining down on the roads for quite a few hours now”, igniting new fires.

It was fuelled by extreme heat and high winds on what became the UK’s hottest day of the year – and the 40-acre blaze quickly escalated into a major incident.

The fast-moving fire spread across local roads and destroyed six residential homes, while three firefighters and a child were taken to hospital, as well as six further people needing treatment for smoke inhalation.



Jane, whose house backs directly onto the golf course where some of the worst damage was seen, told BBC Radio 4’s Today Programme: “The police knocked our door and said that everyone had to be evacuated quickly because they thought the fire was changing directions, and they didn’t know which direction it was going in.

“So, it was literally grab what you need and get out.

“And within about four or five minutes, the police knocked the door again and said: ‘You really have got to get out now’.



“So, get out we did with the cat and away to go to our son’s house.”

Where are the fires raging? AS temperatures soar, several huge wildfires are ravaging the UK, many consuming entire homes, cars and forests. Several blazes are burning in the West Midlands, including in: Stourbridge

Around a hundred firefighters are tackling a massive, out-of-control grass and woodland fire on Racecourse Lane, right by the Stourbridge golf course. Multiple homes have caught fire. Salford Priors, Stratford-upon-Avon Another major incident has been declared as a blaze rages in Warwickshire. Druids Heath

Fire looks like it has broken out on land near Manningford Road and Pennyacre Road in the Druids Heath area of Birmingham. Solihull

A localised outdoor blaze has broken out, drawing responsive fire apparatus to contain it before it spreads to adjacent hedges. In other parts of England, fires rage in: Rainham

A car fire spread rapidly into the roadside grass fencing. The incident has caused traffic chaos, with Ferry Lane being closed both ways. Mousehold Heath, Norwich A major fire in woodland has sent plumes of smoke over Norwich and shut down roads in the city. And seven major wildfires are burning in South Wales, with hotspots including: Porth (Rhondda) A new fire is raging heavily next to residential properties, forcing crews to aggressively drench homes. Blaenavon (Cwmavon Woods) A massive hill and woodland blaze has been burning for days. Fires are also actively spreading through Merthyr Tydfil, Rudry Forestry, Mountain Ash (Cefn Pennar), and Newport.

Jane added: “Just literally 200 yards away from us, we could see the flames from our bedroom window.

“They were well above the rooftops of all the houses that had been evacuated, so you could just see the extent of it.

“It was spreading so fast and going in quite a few different directions across the fields.”



There were multiple wildfires reported across the Midlands yesterday, including also in Stoke-on-Trent, Birmingham, Warwickshire and Worcestershire – as well as others in Norfolk and Wales.



Prime Minister Mr Burnham wrote on X: “Awful to see homes and communities hit by fires across the country tonight as the heatwave continues.

“My thoughts are with everyone affected, particularly those who have been injured or forced from their homes, and with the firefighters who have been taken to hospital.”

The PM also said he will be “speaking to emergency service on the ground”, as he paid tribute to the firefighters working through “incredibly difficult conditions” to bring the wildfires under control.

He thanked emergency services, adding: “Our firefighters are working in incredibly difficult conditions and putting themselves at risk to keep others safe.”



Chair of the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) Phil Garrigan told BBC Radio 4’s Today Programme: “It’s not just the Stourbridge incident that we’ve dealt with over the last 24 hours.

“We’ve had 11 major incidents declared across the UK – Stourbridge particularly, but Sandwell, Pershore, Stoke-on-Trent. We’ve got incidents still raging in Hampshire, in South Wales.

“It’s been a particularly difficult, busy period for the fire and rescue service, where we’ve been under significant pressure.

“Firefighters have been on the front line of climate change for a number of years. They’re doing their absolute best to protect communities and properties.”



Asked whether people were being encouraged on social media to start fires, Mr Garrigan said: “If people are encouraged to, and when people take those kind of directions and start fires, and those fires have an impact that they’ve had in West Midlands – then the individuals who have caused those fires will find themselves behind bars.

“I would be certainly discouraging them from taking any action and following any direction from anyone online, or anyone else for that matter.”

West Midlands Fire Service this morning said crews were “making progress” and “tactically working across several different areas of the site.”



West Midlands Fire Service Chief fire officer Simon Tuhill said last night the Stourbridge fire presented “some of the most challenging conditions ever seen in my 28 years of service”, adding that “the devastation is extensive”.

Tuhill added it was “one of the most significant” incidents the service has ever dealt with as it fielded “thousands of 999 calls”.

He stressed the service will work with cops to determine exactly how the blaze began – though it is believed to have started in dry grass before spreading to houses.

One witness said the monster blaze was “like something from a horror movie”.

Cops urged the public to only ring 999 where absolutely necessary and stay away from the area as crews worked to bring the flames under control.



Local councillor Andrew Troman described the scenes as “apocalyptic”.

Firefighters raced to the scene after being alerted to the inferno around 1.30pm.

The fire is thought to have started in grass near a golf course and jumped the road where it spread fast to homes.

Entire houses were seen consumed by flames in horror images from the scene as around a hundred firefighters tackled the huge wildfire yesterday.

A trackside fire near Stourbridge cancelled all trains with dramatic video showing the inferno burning fiercely by the rails.



Residents of the West Midlands were urged yesterday to stay inside as thick smoke filled the skies.

It had “several points of origin”, the fire service said, warning of closed roads and fallen trees.

The fire service said the blaze covers “from Moreton Road to Iverley Lane, along the total length of Racecourse Lane from Norton Road to County Lane, and from Racecourse Lane to Worcester Lane”.

The M6 northbound was temporarily shut between J5 and J6, where “thick smoke (was) blowing across the carriageway”.

A huge blaze burning by the motorway kept reigniting, National Highways said.



Traffic was backed up for at least six miles and delays in the area were running at more than two hours.

In Castle Vale, Birmingham, a woman was seriously injured as a blaze tore through several homes.

Houses have been evacuated in Goldenhill, Sandyford and Stoke-on-Trent, the fire service said.

Other blazes have broken out in Druids Heath, Birmingham and Solihull.

West Midlands mayor Richard Parker called the fires an “extremely worrying and fast moving situation”.



Seven Trent water even warned of disruption to water supplies as firefighters used all they can from hydrants to battle the blazes.

And a major incident was declared in the Warwickshire area, near Stratford-upon-Avon.

Another major incident was declared in Mousehold Heath, Norwich, as flames ripped through woodland and threatened nearby homes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In Rainham, a car fire quickly spread, igniting roadside fencing and causing traffic chaos.

A blaze in Pershore, Worcestershire has now been brought under control – but 200 properties have been left without power, with one person treated for smoke inhalation.

News.title: Petition to stop PC Harper’s killers being released early from prison hits one million signatures
News.content:
A PETITION to stop the release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers has reached 1million signatures.

The petition was launched when it was revealed that thugs Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were set to be released just half way through their 13-year sentences.



Cole and Bowers are set to be let out in January next year under Labour’s early release scheme – designed to free up space in the prison system.

But hopes were raised for PC Harper’s furious family when the PM ordered a review of the scheme.



Changes were made including preventing rapists and paedophiles from being let out early — but not including those convicted of manslaughter like Bowers and Cole.

Now, after weeks of confusion, Andy Burnham has said he is “increasingly confident” a way could be found to prevent the thugs being turned loose.



But the PM stopped short of confirming how, or whether the pair will remain locked up.

PC Harper’s mum, Debbie Adlam, blasted the “gut-wrenching” confusion as she revealed Downing Street had called her to claim the PM was doing “everything he can.”



Thames Valley Police Federation chairwoman Aileen O’Connor started the petition calling for Bowers and Cole to be kept inside.

She said that Labour had “sent a deeply troubling message” about the value it placed on police officers.

She accepted, however, that there was now a “glimmer of hope”.

Ms O’Connor’s petition has now reached 1million signatures as fury around the potential release of Bowers and Cole grows.

Speaking earlier this week she said: “Their actions so far have been totally demoralising for all police officers.”



Mr Burnham previously said: “I’ve heard the depth of concern felt across the country about the potential release of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

“Obviously I feel for the family and the anguish they’re going through. What I’ve done since I came into office is push the system every single day to go further.

“I’ve not accepted it’s impossible to do more. I believe there is more that can be done.”

Communities Secretary Angela Rayner said the PM was “really clear” the plan would keep the worst offenders in jail.

Asked if this referred to Cole and Bowers, she said: “Yes.”



Newly-married PC Harper died after getting caught up in a strap attached to the rear of a car.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He was dragged more than a mile as the killers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berks, in 2019.

Bowers and Cole, both 17 at the time of the crime, got 13 years in 2020 after being convicted of manslaughter.

News.title: Man, 67, killed after bungalow destroyed in devastating ‘gas explosion’ is pictured as tributes pour in
News.content:
'NEVER FORGOTTEN' Man, 67, killed after bungalow destroyed in devastating ‘gas explosion’ is pictured as tributes pour in

A MAN who has died after his bungalow was destroyed in a devastating gas explosion has been pictured.

Tributes poured in for Steve Woodward, 67, who has been described as a “friend and neighbour” who will “never be forgotten”.



Steve had been inside his home with his pet dog, Milly the Doberman, when the horror explosion occurred at the property in Newton Longville, Buckinghamshire, on Sunday morning.

Steve sadly died in hospital after he suffered near 85 percent burns to his body during the explosion.



The Wing Sports and Social Club in Leighton Buzzard, where Steve was a member, has set up a fundraising page.

It read: “On Sunday, 9 August, our friend and neighbour Steve’s life changed in an instant when a devastating explosion destroyed his home in Newton Longville Sadly, Steve has now passed away, and we are raising money in his memory to support the things that mattered to him and to give something back in his name.



“Steve was so much more than a member of our club.

“He was a friend, a familiar face, someone who could make people laugh, and a huge part of our club family.



“His loss has left a massive hole in the hearts of everyone who knew him.

“Every donation, no matter how big or small, will mean so much. If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this page so we can reach as many of Steve’s friends, family and wider community as possible.

“Thank you to everyone who has supported Steve, his loved ones and our club throughout this incredibly difficult time.



“Rest peacefully, Steve. You will never be forgotten.

“Thank you for your compassion and support during this heart breaking time.”

Labour MP for Buckingham, Bletchley, Tattenhoe, Winslow and other surrounding villages, Callum Anderson, confirmed the tragic news.

The politician stated: “I am deeply saddened to hear of the death of Stephen Woodward following the gas explosion in Newton Longville last Sunday.

“This is an absolute tragedy, and my thoughts are with Stephen’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time, as well as with all those in the wider community who have been affected or displaced by this devastating incident.



“I know that a joint investigation is currently being carried out by the Health and Safety Executive and Thames Valley Police.

“If you have any information that may be relevant to the investigation, please contact Thames Valley Police, quoting URN 660 and the relevant date.

“My sincere condolences go to everyone impacted by this heart breaking loss.”

The local council parish posted a tribute to Steve, saying: “Our deepest condolences go to Steve’s family and friends.

“He will clearly be very much missed by this community.”



Shocking footage captured the roof of the bungalow rocketing into the sky, before debris rained down on cars below.

Further clips showed the home completely gutted with bricks, planks of wood and furniture scattered around it as a fire continues to burn.

A neighbouring bungalow also appears to have its roof severely damaged, with tiles dangling off it.

Locals told how they could smell smoke and gas following the explosion, but the fire department are yet to confirm the cause.

Residents were evacuated from their homes as engineers from SGN, a gas distribution company, carried out safety checks.



Det Insp Philip Turner-Robson said: “This is a tragic development and our thoughts are with the man’s family and friends at this extremely difficult time.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thames Valley Police is managing a coronial investigation into the circumstances surrounding the explosion and collapse of the property, working jointly with the Health and Safety Executive.

“Our inquiries remain ongoing as we seek to establish the full circumstances of what happened.”

News.title: Farage's by-election victory won't stop questions about finances
News.content:
Nigel Farage did not turn up to savour his victory in the by-election he triggered himself.

Overnight he told a rally of Reform UK supporters he had been advised there was an "organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result" and wanted to avoid being "demeaned and humiliated by nobodies".

When the official result did come in hours later, it confirmed the Reform UK leader had indeed won this by-election convincingly with 22,239 votes, but without any serious opposition after the other main parties did not put up candidate.

Farage's allies say he has been both emboldened and re-energised by this race, and it is not difficult to work out why.

He is clearly popular in the constituency, his party has had a commanding lead in national opinion polls for much of the past 18 months, and he has achieved something remarkable in turning his upstart organisation into a mass-membership movement with a serious chance of getting into government.

But today's result won't stop the Metropolitan Police investigation into donations to Reform UK, questions about Farage's friendship with a convicted fraudster, or the parliamentary investigation into why he did not register a Â£5m gift from a billionaire donor.

And given Farage triggered this race and the result was entirely predictable, what was the point of it all?

News.title: Final day of heatwave for many before weekend cooldown
News.content:
Kew Gardens in London reached 38.1C on Thursday, making it the UK's hottest day of 2026 so far, and the fifth hottest UK day on record.

It is also the second time this year that the temperature has reached 38C, after Lingwood, Norfolk recorded 38.0C on 26 June.

This is only the second time that 38C has been reached twice in the same year - the previous occasion being 2022.

Though the Met Office amber warning for extreme heat that covered large swathes of England on Thursday expired at midnight, high temperatures will linger in central and eastern parts of England on Friday.

Long spells of sunshine will lift temperatures to 29-34C (84-93F) across large parts of the Midlands, Lincolnshire, East Anglia and the south-east.

For many places it will mark a third consecutive day above official heatwave thresholds.

The heat will ease elsewhere.

Somewhat cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will generally remain above the norm for the time of year - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.

Many places will be dry with a mix of cloud and sunny spells although a few showers are possible, and these could be heavy and thundery in some places.

News.title: NHS service admits data breach due to pager use
News.content:
The sensitive medical data of transplant patients from across the UK was routinely sent over an unencrypted pager network, an NHS service has admitted.

A BBC investigation found NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) sent the names, dates of birth and types of organs being offered or needed to members of hospital transplant teams who were using pagers, unaware they were not encrypted.

In 2019, then-Health Secretary Matt Hancock announced the NHS in England should stop using pagers by 2021, but some parts of the organisation have continued doing so.

NHSBT said it was "deeply sorry" and has reported the data breach to the Information Commissioner. It added it has now stopped sending patient data in this way.

Pagers are small battery operated radio receivers - popular in the 1980s and 1990s - that can receive short text messages, numbers to call, or alerts.

They are a one-way communication system and only able to receive messages, not send them, which was why they largely fell out of public use as more and more people started carrying mobile phones.

News.title: Watch: What happens if Luigi Mangione pleads guilty?
News.content:
The case of Luigi Mangione, who is accused of killing United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson in New York, is back in the spotlight.

His lawyers are preparing to meet federal prosecutors for a potential plea agreement, according to reports in US media.

Mangione faces two federal charges of stalking resulting in death, each carrying a maximum sentence of life in prison. It was not immediately clear which charges are under discussion.

He also faces a separate state trial over Thompson's death. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges in both cases.

The BBC's Nada Tawfik explains what could happen next.

Read more

News.title: New Zealand breaks ranks and withdraws Infantino support
News.content:
New Zealand have broken rank with Oceania's football governing body to become the latest nation to withdraw support for Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

Infantino has lost support from three regional confederations - Europe's Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf (North and Central America and the Caribbean) - over his aborted plans to sell 20% of the World Cup's commercial rights to private investors.

The Confederation of African Football (Caf) and South American governing body Conmebol have backed the 56-year-old to win a fourth presidential term at the Fifa Congress in March.

New Zealand have followed several individual member nations including England, Wales, Norway, the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland in confirming they will not support Infantino's re-election bid.

"New Zealand Football is also seeking an independent review of the steps undertaken to develop the Fifa Forward Enterprise Scheme (FFE)," a statement read.

"After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust.

"NZF believes this point in time represents an opportunity for all Fifa member associations to advocate for stronger governance, accountability and transparency which are fundamental in maintaining confidence of the administration of the global game."

New Zealand was the only one of the OFC's 11 members to qualify for the 2026 Fifa World Cup, while fellow members New Caledonia have reaffirmed their support for Infantino.

Concacaf members Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have gone against their federation and backed Infantino, while Argentina are aligned with Conmebol in their support.

NZF chief executive Andrew Pragnell said: "We've called for an independent review specifically because what we don't want to see is a sort of in-house quick washover of this.

"An independent review is something else that has been called for by other confederations that will help restore some of the trust."

The Oceania Football Confederation said it welcomed Fifa's decision to withdraw the proposal, but stopped short of declaring or withdrawing support for Infantino.

"The OFC Executive Committee welcomes Fifa's decision to withdraw the FFE proposal and its commitment to review the issues surrounding the project," the statement said.

"The OFC recognises the progress achieved over the last decade in advancing football development in Oceania under Fifa's leadership and encourages Fifa to use the review as an opportunity to identify and implement any changes that may be necessary."

News.title: BBC Verify speaks to woman who filmed ICE agent pointing gun at her
News.content:
A video showing a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent pointing his gun at a woman has been viewed by millions after she shared the moment on Instagram.

Carolina Molina says she was out delivering business cards in Falls Church, Virginia, when she saw ICE agents, who then surrounded her car.

The US Department of Homeland Security said she "attempted to harm officers by weaponising her vehicle". Molina denies this.

BBC Verify assesses the dashcam footage shared by Molina. Jake Horton reports.

Produced by Tom Joyner. Graphics by Mark Edwards.

News.title: You got hold of eclipse glasses just in time - here's what to do with them now
News.content:
Millions of us were treated to a stunning spectacle on Wednesday during mainland Europe's first total solar eclipse for more than 25 years.

And for some in the UK, it was a race against time to find a pair of eye-protecting eclipse glasses as shortages grew.

If you did manage to grab some, you might be asking - what do I do with them now?

"Eclipse glasses are a great example of our single-use culture," says Dr Renee Tonkin, the founder of Science Owl, an environmental education organisation focused on waste.

"Particularly because they're difficult to recycle due to their mixed materials."

According to Recycle Now, which advises on appropriate places to recycle items, the glasses are not wholly recyclable in your household waste.

It says you can recycle the cardboard frames so long as you separate them from the lenses, which are harder to recycle.

So here are three things you can do with those retina-saving spectacles.

News.title: 'Two out of four, baby' - Hunt wins 200m as she eyes historic quadruple
News.content:
Britain's Amy Hunt charged to 200m glory to secure her second gold medal of the European Championships - but the sprinter has her sights set on a historic quadruple in Birmingham.

The 24-year-old wants to "be iconic" and become the first athlete to win four European gold medals at the same championship.

And after triumphing in the 100m on Monday, she added another gold to her collection with a season's best time of 22.19 seconds in the 200m final on Thursday.

Hunt reeled in rival and compatriot Asher-Smith down the back straight to cross the line first.

"Two out of four, baby!" Hunt told BBC TV.

"This is becoming a magical week and one I will remember for the rest of my life."

Hunt is set to compete in the women's and mixed 4x100m relay events later and says there will be "no celebrations and no champagne until Sunday night".

"I have got a debt to the ladies," she said.

"We have got to come out here and make sure we show them who the best sprinting nation is in Europe."

Asher-Smith was beaten to silver by just 0.01 seconds by Ireland's Rhasidat Adeleke, who set a new national record.

"It unfolded exactly how I thought it would," two-time European 200m silver medallist Nethaneel Mitchell-Blake said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I knew Dina would run a blistering bend and then say 'Amy, come and catch me'. And that's what Amy has done."

News.title: 'She was just Gaynor from up the road' - villagers ready for emotional Bonnie Tyler goodbye
News.content:
There aren't many villages where you can walk into a jewellers, a hardware shop, or a cafe, and hear stories about one of the world's biggest music icons.

But in Mumbles, Swansea, Bonnie Tyler was never treated like a superstar.

To many local people, she was Gaynor Sullivan, or "Gaynor who lived up the road".

The Total Eclipse of the Heart singer, who died in July aged 75, would often be seen doing her shopping or having a drink with friends.

On Wednesday it seemed only fitting that the iconic song could be heard playing throughout the village as the biggest partial solar eclipse in nearly three decades took place, with Spotify streams of it almost doubling.

As locals prepare to say goodbye to Tyler, who split her time between the Mumbles and a home in Portugal, it's ordinary moments that people seem to remember most.

On Saturday, hundreds of people are expected to line the streets of Newton Road to pay their respects, as Tyler's coffin makes its way through the village to her home on Mumbles Road.

A service will then be held in St Mary's Church in Swansea city centre on Monday, for family and invited guests, before the cortege makes its way to her birthplace of Skewen, Neath Port Talbot.

News.title: Brothers injured by 'exploding' steam room door
News.content:
Two children from Harrogate were hurt after a steam room door shattered while they were in Turkey on a package holiday.

The brothers, who were 11 and 16 at the time of the incident, were staying at the Green Nature Diamond Hotel with their parents. CCTV footage sourced from the hotel by their father shows the moment the glass door shattered, leaving them with cuts to various parts of their bodies.

Jet2Holidays initially denied liability, but later agreed to pay Â£7,000 compensation to the family.

The travel company said: "We would like to reiterate how sorry we are about this incident."

News.title: Ice cream man hit with noise complaint over van's music
News.content:
An ice cream man has been hit with a noise complaint by someone who did not like the loud chimes from his van.

Mark Edwards was contacted by the council after a Tonyrefail resident complained about the van's music being played in the evening.

He said he had been serving the area for more than 20 years without a complaint and was determined "not to let one individual spoil it for everybody else". He has agreed with customers to beep his horn in each street so they know he is there.

Rhondda Cynon Taf council said it received a noise complaint in June relating to music being played after 20:00 BST, which it investigated and found to be valid.

Edwards, from Trebanog, was taken aback when he found a letter from the council on the van's dashboard: "Twenty-odd years and I have never had anything like this at all. It's unbelievable."

He said his employer told him to stop operating in the area because continuing to use the chimes could result in a fine, but he did not want to stop serving customers, so came up with the alternative plan.

"I thought 'I'm not going to let one individual to spoil it for everybody else', so have come to an arrangement with my customers in the area.

"They know roughly what time I'm there and I toot the horn in each street, and they all come out and enjoy it. They're not going to beat me."

The council said the law required a 19:00 cut-off time for ice cream van operators to use their chimes, but it did not "prevent them from trading after this time".

It said Edwards had been sent a letter reminding him of these requirements and that it considers the matter closed.

News.title: It's in my soul - actor brings small town novel to big screen
News.content:
While the story itself is a work of fiction, McMenamin said the world of Skintown is very much based on his own personal experiences of a teenager growing up during the Troubles in Northern Ireland and trying to escape that.

"The world is mine, and that of my friends we grew up in," he explained.

"The escapism of the rave, and the communities, the kids coming together and realising that they have more in common than they thought.

"It is a work of fiction but there is a lot of me in it."

The soundtrack will also help transport the audience back in time with Prodigy, Elastica, Happy Mondays and Carl Cox featuring.

Despite starring Derry Girls' O'Donnell and Tara Lynne O'Neill, McMenamin said that's where the comparisons end with Lisa McGee's hit show, which was also set during the same period in Northern Ireland.

"The humour is the same," he said. "If we've landed anything half as well as Lisa McGee, we will be over the moon.

"It's the same era and some of the humour will definitely be the same tone â as that's our sense of humour.

"That's the thing about the film I'm proudest about - the humour.

"There's a lot of the film which is very serious, it has a very serious message and it's quite a heavy drama at times but it's also a good night out and the boys in it are brilliant. It's good fun."

News.title: Top grades rise again as students get A-level, T-level and BTec results
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland have opened their A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.

The percentage of top A-level grades edged up again, and a record number of students found out they had secured a place at university.

The cost of going to university has been in the spotlight this year, with mounting pressure on the government to reform student loan repayments, and there has been a renewed focus on technical education under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

But the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged students to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

The percentage of A* and A grades at A-level increased to 28.5% across England, Wales and Northern Ireland this year, up from 28.3% last year.

About 40% of 18-year-olds in England receive A-levels every summer.

Around 250,000 grades for vocational and technical qualifications were also released to students in England.

These include BTec National, Cambridge Technical, Cambridge Advanced National and T-level results.

Almost 20,000 students completed a T-level in 2026, with a pass rate of over 90%.

Launched in 2020, T-levels are two-year technical courses that are taken after GCSEs. They focus more on practical subjects than academic ones, but are an equivalent qualification to three A-levels.

AS-levels, which will count towards students' final A-level results next summer in Wales and Northern Ireland, have also been released.

This year, the pass rate for National 5, Higher and Advanced Higher exams in Scotland rose across the board.

News.title: Son of 102-year-old says father died after being 'pushed off stage'
News.content:
Robert said: "He just asked them to turn the music down."

He said his father turned around to come back down off the stage when he was pushed, and that resulted in a broken hip.

"[That's] the most upsetting part. He wasn't going to live forever but it's not a nice way, obviously in pain," he said.

"We want to see justice, of course.

"They must have known he was an old man. It makes you wonder what the world is coming to.

"It has obviously made it difficult. It would've been nice if he'd gone quietly in his sleep.

"He was in hospital, suffering, for a week-and-a-half. It's not nice.

"I feel sad - even though he could be difficult because of his age and dementia, still, you get used to him being around," he said.

Robert, a retired civil engineer, said his father used to visit the Crow's Nest.

"What happened is not nice. The pub has changed a lot over the years. It has become a youngsters' pub," he said.

Robert said he grew up in the home in the the Llanyrafon neighbourhood where his father had lived since 1960.

He said his dad had a career as a design draughtsman and had lived alone since his wife died 40 years ago.

"Me and my brother would visit our father regularly, and clean the house and buy him food.

"His eyesight had deteriorated and he had been diagnosed with dementia two or three years ago."

Robert said: "He's well-known around here, although a lot of his generation are gone," he added.

He said his father would visit the pub two or three times a week, where he would drink beers, and described how he became a familiar face to some locals.

"I suppose he became a pub character," he added.

News.title: Couple tie the knot on 'magical' solar eclipse day
News.content:
Wednesday's full eclipse may be something many of us remember for a long time: the special glasses, the colanders, and the eerie shadowing of the sun.

And for one couple, it was especially unforgettable as they got married during the once-in-a-generation event.

Jerry and Jamie Bone, from Gosfield, Essex, planned their big day around the astronomical phenomenon - the first total solar eclipse visible over mainland Europe since 1999 - and tied the knot in Alpheton, near Sudbury, Suffolk.

Jamie said they had realised a few years ago the eclipse would take place in 2026, and decided it would be the "perfect" day to get married.

More than 1,500 London bus drivers have walked out today (Friday 13 August) over poor working conditions in hot weather.

Industrial action by members of the Unite union employed by Arriva North London began at 4am this morning and will run until 4.30am on Saturday 15 August.

The following bus services will be impacted: 19, 29, 34, 41, 66, 67, 76, 102, 103, 121, 141, 149, 150, 158, 175, 191, 192, 217, 221, 243, 248, 254, 259, 279, 307, 313, 329, 341, 349, 370, 375, 377, 616, 675, SL1, SL2, W3, W4. W6, N19, N29, N41, N279.

The drivers are taking 26 days of action over what they say is Arriva North London’s failure to act on working conditions during extreme heat.

Drivers from eight bus garages – Barking, Edmonton, Enfield, Grays, Palmers Green, Stamford Hill, Tottenham and Wood Green – are involved in the dispute.

Planned strikes in August and September will coincide with closures on the Piccadilly line, with significant delays and cancellations expected.

The union says that most Arriva buses operate with air cooling systems rather than air conditioning, leaving drivers exposed to extreme temperatures during the recent series of heatwaves.

Unite is calling on Arriva to fit all buses with effective air conditioning, arguing that working in scorching temperatures is dangerous for drivers, whose cabs can reach highs of more than 40 degrees. Such temperatures can cause health issues including heatstroke and exhaustion, fatigue, dehydration and dizziness.

Unite general secretary Sharon Graham said: “The heatwave this week has caused even more problems for our members at Arriva North London, who have once again faced doing a demanding job in unbearable conditions.

“No worker should be made ill by their job. This problem is raised year after year and as the summers get hotter it can no longer be swept under the carpet. Arriva can afford to act on this serious issue, which puts both drivers and the general public at risk and it must make this a priority.”

The industrial action comes after a summer in which the UK has struggled with drought and extreme heat.

On Thursday, 13 August, the Met Office reported the hottest day of the year so far with temperatures surging to 38.1C at Kew Gardens in West London.

“Extreme heat is creating challenges across many sectors, including London's bus network,” Wasim Mohammed, managing director of Arriva London, told The Independent.

“The wellbeing of our colleagues and customers is our top priority, and we are working closely with Transport for London to ensure appropriate support is in place.

“We have already introduced additional support for drivers during hot weather, including regular breaks and welfare checks – and are continuing to invest in long-term improvements, including upgraded air conditioning systems and new buses coming into our fleet.

“These upgrades are complex and being led by TfL as part of its extreme heat taskforce. We urge Unite to come back to the negotiating table and engage with us constructively so we can avoid further disruption.”

The Independent has contacted Transport for London for comment.

Australian golf prodigy Jessica Bang has died at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage.

Bang was preparing for a tournament in Thailand when she collapsed on 1 August.

She was rushed to hospital for emergency brain surgery but after nearly two weeks in intensive care, she passed away on Thursday.

Bang won her first professional event in just her fifth start earlier this year, triumphing at the Ford Women’s NSW Open Regional Qualifying Event at Moss Vale.

Bang qualified for the WPGA Tour through Qualifying School at the end of 2025, with victory at the Queensland Amateur capping off an “outstanding amateur career”.

The WPGA Tour of Australia branded Bang as “an outstanding young talent” in their tribute to her.

“The WPGA Tour of Australasia and the broader Australian golf community is deeply saddened by the passing of young Tour member Jessica Bang in Thailand,” a statement read.

“The thoughts and prayers of everyone at the WPGA Tour of Australasia and the broader Australian golf community are with Jessica’s family, friends and all those who knew and loved her at this incredibly difficult time.“

Bang qualified for the WPGA Tour through Qualifying School at the end of 2025, with victory at the Queensland Amateur capping off an “outstanding amateur career”.

A GoFundMe was set up by Bang’s cousins to help cover medical expenses, which has so far raised nearly 50,000 Australian dollars (£26,000).

Her family members announced Bang’s death on the fundraiser page, writing: "We are truly heartbroken by this news.

“However, we would like to continue to remember Jessica and celebrate her achievements, passion, and dedication to golf.

“As her cousins, we will forever cherish the time and memories we shared with Jessica. Her sense of humour, together with her cheerful and vibrant personality, will always be remembered and treasured by our family.

“The funds we have raised will be given to her parents to help contribute towards her medical expenses.

“Once again, we would like to express our deepest gratitude to everyone who has supported Jessica and our family through this incredibly difficult time.”

A dog in California has been euthanized even though the case to save the pet reached the Supreme Court.

The legal battle over the fate of a three-year-old Great Pyrenees and German Shepherd mix named Bruce started in March following a series of biting episodes.

On four separate occasions from February 2024 to February 2026, Bruce attacked passersby, causing injuries including “severe disfiguring lacerations,” according to Ventura County Animal Services. In one instance on November 4, 2025, a woman was walking in her apartment complex when Bruce bit her on the forearm, requiring her to get surgery and skin grafts.

Animal Services said it had petitioned for Bruce to be declared vicious to “protect public safety,” and on March 26, a hearing officer agreed and ordered the dog to be euthanized.

After months of Bruce’s owners and the Santa Paula Animal Rescue Center fighting for Bruce’s life in court, he was euthanized on Wednesday. Dan Bolton, a lawyer for the owners and rescue center, told The Independent he was “appalled” by Bruce’s euthanasia.

open image in gallery Bruce, a three-year-old Great Pyrenees and German Shepherd mix from California, has been euthanized over several biting episodes ( Dan Bolton )

“We do not take the loss of an animal’s life lightly. We have compassion for Bruce and for those who care about him, just as we have compassion for those who were injured,” Animal Services said in a Tuesday statement. “Our responsibility is to follow the law, comply with court orders, and fulfill our mandate to protect the community.”

After Bruce’s owner, Claire Birgy, appealed the hearing officer’s determination that the dog was vicious, a Ventura County Superior Court judge affirmed in an April 15 ruling that Bruce was vicious and must be euthanized within a month.

But the issue was tied up in court until the United States District Court denied an emergency application seeking to block the Superior Court’s order, which allowed Animal Services to proceed with Bruce’s euthanasia.

open image in gallery Animal Services said it had petitioned for Bruce to be declared vicious to ‘protect public safety,’ but his supporters argued there were other options than euthanasia ( Dan Bolton )

The case moved all the way up to the Supreme Court, but not in time to save Bruce. A day after Bruce was euthanized, the Supreme Court denied an emergency application seeking to reinstate a temporary pause on the Superior Court’s order.

“At the time Bruce was euthanized, there was no court order in place preventing the County from complying with the Ventura County Superior Court’s April 15th order,” Animal Services said on Wednesday.

Attorney Bolton compared Bruce to an inmate on Death Row.

“Bruce was killed yesterday despite the pendency of our emergency application to the United States Supreme Court to preserve his life...If a death row inmate filed a similar stay, the State would never proceed to execute that person until the Court ruled on the stay,” Bolton told The Independent.

“The utter disregard for the judicial process in the United States Supreme Court, and shameful disrespect for Bruce’s life, is truly sickening,” the lawyer added.

open image in gallery On four separate occasions from February 2024 to February 2026, Bruce attacked passersby, causing injuries including “severe disfiguring lacerations,” according to Ventura County Animal Services ( Google Earth )

The Santa Paula Animal Rescue Center grieved Bruce in a Facebook post Thursday.

“For months, SPARC fought to bring Bruce back under its protection. We sought legal relief. We supported emergency filings. We identified safe placement options. We offered to pay. We offered to assume responsibility,” the rescue center wrote.

“We are heartbroken for Bruce, for his family…and for every rescue worker who knows what it means to fight for a dog the system has already decided to give up on,” the post continued.

Winona Birgy-Krasnoff, the daughter of Bruce's owner, said the family was not proposing a solution where the public would ever be exposed to the dog.

"Our agenda was that Bruce got to live out his natural life in a way where he was protected from the public, and the public was protected from him,” Birgy-Krasnoff told ABC 7.

More than one million people have signed a petition to block two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers from being released from prison early following huge public outcry.

Thames Valley Police Federation (TVPF) launched the petition last week, condemning the government’s decision not to include the killers in exceptions from a new early prison scheme as “outrageous”.

PC Harper, 28, was responding to reports of a quad bike theft in Berkshire in 2019 when he was caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter, are set to be freed in January - half way through their sentences - under existing plans.

Downing Street has faced significant backlash after it announced some offenders, including the most serious sex offenders, would be exempt from plans to release some prisoners early - but did not include those who have killed first responders.

open image in gallery PC Andrew Harper was killed while on duty in 2019 ( Thames Valley Police )

On Tuesday, prime minister Andy Burnham said he is “increasingly confident” that work to increase space in the prison system “will allow us to reduce the number of people released early and, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC Harper, prevent their early release altogether”.

Mr Burnham said justice secretary Alex Norris will now look at ways to keep “a greater number of the most serious offenders” behind bars and will announce the plans when Parliament returns in September.

In the petition, Aileen O'Connor, chair of the TVPF, said the government’s decision “pours salt into wounds that have never healed”.

open image in gallery Pc Andrew Harper’s mother Debbie Adlam said a Downing Street official had spoken to her ( PA )

“It is an insult to Andrew's family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family,” she added.

The petition has attracted hundreds of comments from supporters, including from current and former officers.

“As an ex TVP officer, it disgusts me the lack of support towards officers, one wrote. “Officers put their life or the line day in, day out and should be going back to their families at the end of the shift. It should be life for life no matter the circumstances but taking a life of an emergency service worker and getting released early is not definitely not okay. I am so angry and my heart goes out to all of his family.”

Another added: “No family should have to face this, least of all the family of a man dedicated to protecting us.”

PC Harper’s mother said she had received a call from Downing Street on Monday night and has “got a little bit of hope that we didn’t have before” that the killers will not be released early.

Discussing the call she had with a member of the prime minister’s staff, Debbie Adlam told BBC Breakfast: “She said that he wanted to convey that he wants to do everything that he can and has more hope now of finding a resolution to this to try and keep them in prison.

“I think the fact that it’s actually come from Downing Street – I’ve got to try and have some faith in it but, at the same time, I have to protect my own feelings.”

open image in gallery Jessie Cole (left) and Albert Bowers, two of Pc Andrew Harper’s killers ( Thames Valley Police )

But she added: “It feels like a hash. It feels like a rush job. It feels like nobody’s put enough effort into actually look for reasons or ways.

“We are having to push on every level, and it just doesn’t feel like, as a British citizen, I shouldn’t be doing this. They weren’t given extreme sentences, and I’m only asking for them to do what they were given.”

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson previously said: “The death of PC Andrew Harper was a horrific crime. Our thoughts are with his family and friends, and we share the anger from the police community that we are in this position.

“Thanks to tireless campaigning by Andrew’s family, Harper’s Law means that anyone convicted of killing an emergency worker whilst committing a crime now gets a mandatory life sentence. This government has gone further by introducing a presumption that anyone convicted of murdering a police, prison or probation officer is handed a whole-life order.

“We have been clear that we wanted to go further and block more offenders from getting out sooner into their sentence but could not do so without risking prisons reaching capacity and collapsing.

“If that happened, police could not make arrests, courts could not remand offenders and there would be unchecked criminality on our streets.”

News.title: Nicole Kidman admits she was ‘very fearful and deeply vulnerable’ after Keith Urban divorce
News.content:

Nicole Kidman has opened up about her divorce from Keith Urban in a new interview, saying the future is “completely unknown to me right now.”

Kidman quietly filed for divorce from Urban in Nashville last September after 19 years of marriage. By January, the divorce was finalized, citing irreconcilable differences. The couple agreed to share custody of their two daughters (Sunday Rose, 18, and Faith, 15); neither sought spousal support, and they did not have to appear in court.

In a wide-ranging interview for British Vogue’s September issue, Kidman said she was taking a “feelings first” approach to her new single era.

“That’s just who I am. I don’t overthink things and I’m probably not that analytical. I’m far more feeling-centered and I lead with my heart... It throws people, because I think they think I’ll be far more measured and I’m not,” she said.

“I can still approach things intellectually,” she continued, “but my desire is not to be ruled by my head. I’ve always wanted to live a well-examined life, so what does that entail? Trying things, making mistakes, failing, getting back up, moving on, embracing love, staying open, keeping the heart open and the possibilities.”

open image in gallery Nicole Kidman opens up about her post-divorce mindset in ‘British Vogue’s’ September issue ( Venetia Scott/Vogue )

open image in gallery Kidman told ‘British Vogue’ she’s moving ‘forward with an enormous amount of hope’ ( Venetia Scott/Vogue )

Nevertheless, Kidman admitted it had not been the easiest year. “But at the same time I’m like, ‘OK, I didn’t expect this. I had a different view of what my life was going to be, but this is what it is now.’ You make all these plans and you have all these ideas of what it’s all going to be like and then it’s… not. You have to adjust. You adapt. The future, it’s completely unknown to me right now.”

Asked if she found the uncertainty of her future scary, Kidman replied: “There was a point where I was very fearful and deeply vulnerable, which is exposing. And then at the same time [I’m] going, ‘Well, I can either really not confront it and just curl up, or I can just go forward with an enormous amount of hope.’”

Both hailing from Australia, Kidman and Urban met in Los Angeles in 2005 and married in Sydney the following year.

open image in gallery Nicole Kidman quietly filed for divorce from Keith Urban last year after 19 years of marriage ( AFP/Getty )

It was Urban’s first marriage and Kidman’s second, following her marriage to Tom Cruise from 1990 to 2001.

Kidman has recently been linked to LA-based private equity investor named Michael Reinstein. The two were spotted having a conversation on the balcony of her Portofino, Italy, hotel last month. She has not commented publicly on the nature of their relationship.

See the full feature on Kidman in the September issue of British Vogue, available via digital download and on newsstands from Thursday 20th August.
