World.title: Colombia says 377 still missing three days after 7.4M earthquake
World.content:
The director of Colombia’s disaster management agency UNGRD said Thursday that at least 273 people died and that 377 were missing from the region that was struck by a 7.4M earthquake on Monday.

According to UNGRD director David Tamayo, the earthquake affected a total of 97,515 people.

So far, rescue workers and neighbors were able to rescue 348 people from the rubble alive and 3,826 people were injured.

The earthquake, which was the strongest in a decade, destroyed 12,563 homes and damaged another 75,654.

At least 172 apartment buildings collapsed, said Tamayo.

Damaged public infrastructure

217 health centers and hospitals

2,206 educational facilities

825 community centers

226 roads

71 aqueducts

24 vehicular bridges

8 pedestrian bridges

5 airports

The disaster triggered President Abelardo de la Espriella to declare an economic emergency in the disaster area, and in the southern Putumayo and the eastern Norte de Santander province where no damages were reported.

This State of Exception allows the president to govern by decree when it comes to matters related to disaster relief and reconstruction in the affected area.

The State of Exception will last three months and can be extended by another three with congressional approval.

World.title: Colombia declares economic emergency to rebuild after earthquake
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella said he would declare an economic emergency and create a reconstruction fund for homes and small businesses that were destroyed in Monday’s earthquake.

In a press statement, De la Espriella said that the government would initially support victims with temporary relief and will declare an economic emergency to find the funds for reconstruction.

Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said the government was not yet considering raising taxes to find the approximately COP20 trillion ($6.4 billion) that would at least be needed for reconstruction.

The president said his government would initially prioritize relief for the estimated 24,000 families from the west of the country who have lost their homes or businesses.

The temporary relief measures would include:

The payment of public services for affected families by the government.

Housing rent subsidies for those who lost their homes.

Tax and financial relief measures.

Economic support for the most vulnerable families.

Support mechanisms for merchants and small business owners who have been affected by the earthquake.

As part of the emergency, De la Espriella announced the creation of a “Miracle Fund, an entity that will channel national and international contributions destined for the reconstruction of hospitals, educational centers, properties, roads, and airports that suffered damage from the earthquake.”

“The state of emergency must encompass economic reactivation measures that stimulate investment, reduce obstacles to project development, and generate more jobs in the affected areas,” said the president.

An economic emergency gives the president three months to issue decrees related to the cause of the emergency without having to go through Congress.

The legal validity of the decree declaring an emergency and those that follow will only be tested by the Constitutional Court.

At the time of publication the President’s Office had yet to issue its first decree.

World.title: Colombia asked US to carry out joint military operations: Hegseth
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella asked the US Government for joint military operations “to destroy terrorists and terror networks,” said US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth Wednesday.

At an event of the so-called Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (ACCC) in Panama, Hegseth said that “Colombia will join the ACCC, becoming the 19th member.”

Through the newly inaugurated president, as our president likes to say “President El Tigre,” Colombia has already requested that our department of war join Colombia in its fight against narcoterrorism. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth

Hegseth’s announcement was rejected by leftist opposition party Historic Pact, whose Senate chief Ivan Cepeda said that “the US citizen Abelardo de la Espriella wants to surrender our government, our territory and our sovereignty to the strategic interests of the United States.

Cepeda stressed that Colombia’s constitution allows only the Senate to permit the entry of foreign troops to the country.

Colombia’s sovereignty is not up for negotiation, it is not to be surrendered, and it cannot be subordinated to the military interests of any foreign power. To defend it is to defend the dignity of the nation, the independence of the Republic, and the right of the Colombian people to freely decide on their territory and their destiny. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Ahead of taking office on Friday, De la Espriella said that he would join US-led alliances that allegedly seek to combat drug trafficking.

In his inaugural speech, the president said he intends to “defeat, without truce, narco-terrorism and all criminal organizations that threaten the freedom of Colombia.”

The State Department last week announced that it would seek to send a $1 billion military aid package to Colombia to “support the De la Espriella Administration’s efforts to defeat the vicious narcoterrorist and criminal organizations that threaten US, Colombian, and hemispheric security and economic prosperity.”

World.title: Controversy in Colombia over refusal to allow foreign search and rescue teams
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella has been criticized over its refusal to accept foreign search and rescue workers in the crucial hours after Monday’s earthquake.

One of the first to raise the alarm was China’s ambassador to Bogota, Zhu Jingyang, who called on the government on Tuesday to “release the name of the official and his or her designated contact person to coordinate international aid for the earthquake victims.”

El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele said that he was told that Colombia’s “rescue teams, medical personnel, and other emergency responders are on the scene and handling the situation” and “they do not require personnel support.”

Mexico’s President Caudia Sheinbaum said that her government was waiting for approval to send a team of 225 rescue workers to look for survivors, but was waiting for a “formal invitation” from Bogota.

In a response to growing pressure, newspaper El Tiempo said Colombia didn’t need foreign search and rescue teams because “the country has 23 teams with personnel that is part of the global elite.”

The Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday evening that it had “called on the international community to provide support in addressing the emergency, in order to tackle the most severely affected areas and mitigate the disaster.”

But social leader Leonard Renteria from Buenaventura said Wednesday that “as of yesterday, we still didn’t know anything about the arrival of rescue workers” in the partially destroyed port city.

“On the streets, we’ve seen people from the neighborhoods with the firefighters and civil defense personnel,” Renteria posted on social media platform X.

Fifty hours after Monday’s disaster, the US Department of State said it had “mobilized urban search-and-rescue (USAR) technical teams from Fairfax County, Virginia, and Los Angeles County, California to support Colombia’s search and rescue efforts.”

With chances of finding people alive rapidly decreasing, pressure on the government to respond increased online.

“I would really like to know the technical reason for rejecting assistance from teams that specialize in this type of disaster. There are many affected areas and plenty of evidence of technical inadequacies,” said civil engineer Gina Villalobos on X.

According to opposition congresswoman Maria Fernanda Carrascal, “it was an ideological decision, they only wanted rescue workers from Israel and the United States to enter while the Mexicans have been ready since Monday.”

On Wednesday afternoon, newly appointed disaster response chief David Tamayo said the government would also allow search and rescue workers from Ecuador and El Salvador “that can guarantee the provision of search and rescue teams and that are recognized by their own governments as meeting international search and rescue standards.”

These teams would come to search for hundreds of people who are feared to be under the rubble of buildings that collapsed in the worst earthquake in 10 years.

World.title: West Colombia earthquake killed more than 227 people, say local authorities
World.content:
Local and regional authorities have said that at least 227 people were confirmed killed in Monday’s earthquake while search and rescue teams continue to look for survivors.

So far, 120 people were confirmed dead in Valle del Cauca where locals said that entire towns in the north of the province were all but destroyed by the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck the Choco province on Monday.

In Cali, the capital of Valle del Cauca, rescue workers continued to look for survivors under the rubble of apartment buildings that collapsed. Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder imposed a curfew in the city after locals chased him away from a search and rescue operation.

Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba said that mayors from the capital Quibdo and 22 affected towns reported 14 deaths and 140 injuries.

Multiple parts of the western province have yet to be contacted, however, as the local energy and telephone grid were destroyed by the earthquake, said Cordoba.

In Pereira, a city located at only 60 kilometers of the earthquake’s epicenter, and the surrounding Risaralda province, at least 88 people had died and dozens were still missing.

All major cities in the coffee region, Choco and Valle del Cauca declared an emergency to deal with the hundreds of injured that required medical attention at one of the cities’ hospitals.

President Abelardo de la Espriella said Tuesday morning that the earthquake destroyed more than 5,000 homes and that 188 people were missing.

The National Army and fire brigades from across Colombia sent teams to the cities in the disaster area to help with local search and rescue missions.

The US Department of State said it had committed $15.5 million “in funding for emergency shelter, food, protection, and earthquake assessments” for Colombia.

The Chinese embassy in Bogota said that Chinese companies that operate in Colombia were “sending heavy equipment to the most affected areas of the earthquake, participating in rescue efforts and the clearing of debris, in order to rescue the affected population using all available means.”

World.title: Colombia declares national disaster after devastating earthquake
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a national disaster and sent his ministers to the west of Colombia to coordinate rescue operations in response to a 7.4M earthquake.

Following an emergency meeting at disaster management agency UNGRD, De la Espriella said he would travel to Pereira, one of the worst hit cities, to further coordinate the government response.

Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara would coordinate rescue operations for the rest of the coffee region, the health and defense ministers would travel to the Choco and Transport Minister Elsa Noguera would coordinate efforts in Valle del Cauca from Cali.

De la Espriella canceled plans he had to visit La Guajira, a northern province that wasn’t affected by the earthquake.

Throughout the morning, local and regional media reported dozens of collapsed buildings in multiple cities in Valle del Cauca, the coffee region and Choco.

More than 110 people were killed and dozens were injured because of the earthquake, De la Espriella said at a press conference.

The earthquake damaged more than 1,500 homes and destroyed 37. Sixty-one buildings collapsed and 18 healthcare centers suffered damage as well as 52 schools and 17 community centers.

The roof of the Pereira airport also came down and five other airports in western Colombia reported damages, said the president.

According to the National Police, road travel has been complicated because of landslides and fallen trees.

The government has yet to report on missing persons.

“Right now, the most important thing is to protect lives, rescue those who remain trapped, treat the injured, and bring aid to the hardest-hit communities,” said Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo.

“United we will overcome this emergency,” Restrepo added.

The vice-president, together with Foreign Minister Omar Bula, will coordinate foreign aid.

According to the Colombian Geological Service, the earthquake was the strongest in Colombia of the past decade and the strongest in the west of the country since 1979.

World.title: 7.4M earthquake hits western Colombia: at least 110 killed, dozens of buildings collapsed
World.content:
An M7.4 earthquake hit western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 110 people and injuring hundreds.

The earthquake struck around 7:30 and had its epicenter in San Jose del Palmar, a municipality in the Choco province.

In the hour that followed, locals began reporting collapsed buildings in the cities of Cali, Pereira and Manizales, where a tower of the cathedral and a dozen other buildings fully or partially collapsed, according to Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas.

In a first report on fatalities, Risaralda Governor Juan Diego Patiño said that at least 40 people were killed in the capital Perira. Another three would have been killed in Manizales.

In Cali, an unknown number of people would be trapped under the rubble of multiple buildings. At least 27 people would be killed in the Valle del Cauca province.

Large parts of the roof of the Pereira airport came down, according to video shared on social media.

Flights to Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura were suspended while airport authorities check for damages to infrastructure

In Quibdo, the capital of Choco, at least four people were killed and another 69 were injured, Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba said in her second report.

The earthquake was also felt strongly in the capital Bogota and in Medellin where no injuries were reported.

In an initial response, President Abelardo de la Espriella said on social media platform X that he had “personally taken charge of the emergency response in San José del Palmar.”

“I will also be in Pereira in person to stand with those affected and monitor the government’s response,” said De la Espriella, who took office on Friday and has yet to appoint his director of disaster response agency UNGRD.

The president later reported that he was on his way to Bogota to lead rescue efforts from the UNGRD’s main office.

I have established a Unified Command Post at the UNGRD, from where I will personally lead the efforts to assist the communities in Chocó, the Coffee Region, and all affected areas. President Abelardo de la Espriella

According to the Colombian Geological Service, the earthquake was the strongest in Colombia of the past decade.

World.title: US seeks $1B aid package for Colombia’s new government
World.content:
Th US State Department said it will ask Congress for $1 billion for “deepening our shared and economic partnership” with the government of Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

The funding boost, which resembles that of the first year of Plan Colombia in 2000, seeks to “support the De la Espriella Administration’s efforts to defeat the vicious narcoterrorist and criminal organizations that threaten US, Colombian, and hemispheric security and economic prosperity.”

In preliminary talks, De la Espriella had already agreed to join the “Shield of the Americas,” a regional initiative of far-right governments to jointly fight crime.

According to a fact sheet, the funds that would require congressional approval would be used to:

Strengthen Colombia’s security forces

Disrupt illegal armed groups and organized crime’s ability to launder money

Significantly expand coca eradication and cocaine interdiction operations

Halt migration

Increase State presence in conflict regions

Combat child recruitment and exploitation by illegal armed groups

The administration of President Donald Trump also seeks to “increase trade and deepen economic ties between our countries.”

In order to do this, nominated US ambassador Nate Morris told the Senate that De la Espriella would withdraw from a memorandum of understanding with the government of China that sought to improve ties with the Asian giant.

Trump’s aid package would help Colombian communities “recover from potential El Niño-related flooding, drought,” which is expected to cause emergencies between December and March.

The US would also support a Bilateral Prosperity Dialogue to “stabilize” Colombia’s economy, “strengthening its energy generation and distribution sectors, exploring critical mineral investments, and creating new opportunities for US investors.”

The aid package would additionally “strengthen Colombian small and medium enterprises in agribusiness, manufacturing, and tech services by connecting them to US buyers and linking them to U.S.-aligned supply chains.”

The two governments would additionally seek to modernize Colombia’s digital, port and energy infrastructure while “positioning Colombia as a trusted nearshoring partner for supply chain diversification.”

World.title: Argentina's largest investment project aims to export Vaca Muerta gas
World.content:
Argentina's largest investment project aims to export Vaca Muerta gas

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 22:46 UTC Full article

The project seeks to turn gas from the Vaca Muerta formation, in Neuquén province, into liquefied natural gas exports

Argentina's majority state-owned oil company YPF confirmed on Thursday that it has filed an application for the Argentina LNG project to join the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI). The venture, developed alongside Italy's Eni and the Emirati company XRG, contemplates an estimated outlay of 51 billion dollars over its full life, the largest figure submitted so far under the scheme.

The project seeks to turn gas from the Vaca Muerta formation, in Neuquén province, into liquefied natural gas exports. Its design includes gas production in Neuquén, dedicated transport infrastructure, processing plants, liquids fractionation trains and two floating liquefaction units with a combined capacity of 12 million tonnes a year, which will operate off the coast of Río Negro, in the San Matías Gulf, from 2031. The consortium plans to scale up to 18 million tonnes.

“We are talking about a growth platform that will generate employment, technological development, local suppliers and an unprecedented international position for our country,” said Horacio Marín, YPF's chairman and chief executive, in the company's statement, which described joining the scheme as “a fundamental step.”

The RIGI, created under the Ley Bases, grants long-term legal, tax, customs and foreign exchange stability, conditions the company considers essential to attract international financing. The largest project filed under the scheme until now was LLL Oil, at 25 billion dollars, in May.

The investment plan foresees some 5 billion dollars for the initial exploration and drilling phase, and 29 billion over the next five years to bring the two floating units into operation, of which 24 billion corresponds to infrastructure: industrial complexes, dedicated pipelines and port facilities. The company estimates export revenues of close to 10 billion dollars a year over twenty years.

A substantial portion of the financing will be structured through project finance backed by long-term export contracts with investment-grade buyers. JP Morgan is acting as arranger. The first stage amounts to 15.5 billion dollars and, according to Marín, 47 banks submitted offers worth 2.4 times the amount sought.

The company holding the blocks was set up with YPF holding 36% of the capital and Eni and XRG 32% each. XRG is the international investment arm of ADNOC, Abu Dhabi's state oil company. Eni, which leads engineering on the development, placed the final investment decision towards the end of 2026 and described the project as a global leader in liquefied natural gas.

During the construction stage, planned between 2026 and 2030, YPF calculates some 20,000 annual jobs including direct, indirect and induced positions, peaking at up to 40,000 in the third year, and around 8,000 during the operational phase. Contracting of domestic suppliers is estimated at 15 billion dollars.

World.title: Brazil: Two days before the deadline, Bolsonaro's party cannot register Flávio as candidate
World.content:
Brazil: Two days before the deadline, Bolsonaro's party cannot register Flávio as candidate

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 22:34 UTC Full article

“You saw that they falsified my party affiliation. The system will try everything to stop me, but it will not succeed, because God is in command,” Flávio Bolsonaro said

Brazil's Liberal Party was unable on Thursday to file Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy with the Superior Electoral Court, after the electoral system recorded him as a member of a different party. The deadline for submitting candidacies expires on Saturday at 7pm.

A certificate issued by the court at 11:13 on Thursday listed the senator as a regular member of the Missão party since Wednesday, August 12, and recorded his departure from the Liberal Party on the same date. Official records had until then shown continuous membership of the PL since November 2021. The discrepancy blocked the registration procedure. The campaign's legal team also reported that the party temporarily lost credentialed access to the platform used to submit data to the court.

The Superior Electoral Court said in a statement that the change did not result from a breach of its affiliation system but from improper use of the tool by someone holding access credentials, and opened an investigation. The certificate itself specifies that affiliation data is entered into the Filia system under the parties' own responsibility and that the record carries “only a relative presumption of veracity.”

Flávio Bolsonaro released a video on social media. “You saw that they falsified my party affiliation. The system will try everything to stop me, but it will not succeed, because God is in command,” he said. His team requested immediate correction of the record and announced it would ask the Federal Police to open an investigation. The change was reversed hours later.

Missão, whose president and presidential candidate is Renan Santos, said in a statement it had been the victim of a fraudulent affiliation attempt. The party said its own system detected the irregularity and tried to cancel it the same day, a request the court rejected, and announced it would provide authorities and the press with a report containing access logs, emails and IP addresses. “The last thing we want is Flávio Bolsonaro affiliated to Missão,” Santos told the Metrópoles website.

This is not the first such episode. In an earlier case, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva appeared registered as a Liberal Party member in the electoral system. The police investigation concluded the change had been made by a 13-year-old who did not breach the system, according to the same outlet.

By Thursday, six presidential candidacies had been registered, among them that of Santos, who polls at around 3%. Campaigning officially begins on Sunday, with Lula holding an event in São Bernardo do Campo, in greater São Paulo, and Flávio Bolsonaro at Copacabana beach in Rio de Janeiro. The most recent CNT/MDA poll puts the president on 48% against the senator's 39.1% in a potential runoff.

World.title: Colombia faces reconstruction with 96% of the year's debt quota already used
World.content:
Colombia faces reconstruction with 96% of the year's debt quota already used

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 22:31 UTC Full article

De la Espriella said the country is going through “the most complex fiscal crisis in its entire history” and announced that the emergency will allow the creation of the so-called Fondo Milagro

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared an economic emergency on Wednesday to address the consequences of Monday's magnitude 7.4 earthquake in the west of the country, against a backdrop of fiscal constraints that will shape how reconstruction is financed.

The outgoing government used 96% of the domestic debt issuance quota set for this year, an unprecedented proportion in a presidential transition, where the norm was to leave around 30% available for the successor, according to calculations by economist Alejandro Rojas of Banco de Bogotá. The current budget also faces a shortfall of more than 30 trillion pesos, some 9.375 billion dollars.

De la Espriella said the country is going through “the most complex fiscal crisis in its entire history” and announced that the emergency will allow the creation of the so-called Fondo Milagro, intended to channel domestic and international contributions towards rebuilding hospitals, schools, housing, roads and airports. “The emergency will have to include economic reactivation measures,” he said at his first press conference since taking office, at which he took no questions.

The measures announced include the state covering utility bills for affected families, rent subsidies, tax and financial relief, support for traders and small businesses, and assistance for the most vulnerable households. Finance Minister Miguel Gómez Martínez had told congressional economic committees of the possibility of taking out a World Bank loan of up to 450 million dollars and of postponing personal income tax payments by several weeks.

Wednesday's official toll stands at 265 dead, 3,494 injured, 496 missing and 25,872 families affected, with 1,136 homes destroyed, 8,357 damaged and 35 health centers hit. The figures are provisional.

The United States Geological Survey estimates the most likely losses at between one and ten billion dollars, although its upper range contemplates an impact of up to 7% of gross domestic product, equivalent to some 40.6 billion dollars. Gómez had set out to cut state spending by 20 trillion pesos this year, close to 6 billion dollars, a target reconstruction is likely to postpone. “Some of the tax cuts the government wanted will probably have to be put off, and a discussion about additional revenue may even have to be brought to the table,” said José Ignacio López, president of the think tank Anif.

A study by the International Monetary Fund covering 96 emerging economies between 2012 and 2023 concludes that markets do not penalize the earthquake itself but the institutional capacity to respond. Sovereign spreads tend to rise and stay elevated in countries with weaker state capacity, an effect that appears two months after the event and can exceed 60 basis points by the fifth month. In countries that respond effectively, the spread remains stable or even falls.

The declaration of economic emergency temporarily empowers the executive to issue decrees with the force of law and is subject to review by the Constitutional Court. In April the court struck down the emergency decreed by Gustavo Petro, though in different circumstances, after a tax reform failed in Congress. It has, however, upheld the mechanism following the 1999 Eje Cafetero earthquake, the 2010 floods and the 2017 Mocoa landslide.

World.title: Disapproval of Orsi's government climbs to 57% in the third quarter, Opción finds
World.content:
Disapproval of Orsi's government climbs to 57% in the third quarter, Opción finds

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 10:16 UTC Full article

The breakdown shows 30% rating the government's performance as very poor and 27% as poor, against 16% who consider it good and 3% very good

Fifty-seven percent of Uruguayans disapprove of the performance of the government led by Yamandú Orsi and 19% approve, according to the third-quarter 2026 Public Opinion Monitor released on Wednesday by the polling firm Opción. In the previous measurement the figures were 48% and 20% respectively.

The breakdown shows 30% rating the government's performance as very poor and 27% as poor, against 16% who consider it good and 3% very good. Twenty-four percent do not assess it either way and 1% did not answer. The net rating moved from -28 to -38 points.

The president's personal evaluation returns somewhat less negative figures. Twenty-two percent approve of his performance, 28% take neither view and 50% disapprove. His net rating went from -17 to -28 compared with the previous quarter. Orsi's approval is three points above the government's and his disapproval seven points lower.

The series for the term shows a sustained progression. Approval of the government's performance stood at 30% at the start of the mandate, 23% in the first quarter of 2026 and 20% in the second. Disapproval travelled the opposite path: 19%, 38% and 48%. According to the firm's analysis, the main shift lies not in the fall in support but in the contraction of the segment without a settled view, which was 51% at the beginning of the term and is now 24%.

The sharpest movement is within the governing party's own electorate. Among those who voted for the Frente Amplio in the first round of 2024, disapproval rose nine points from the previous quarter, the largest increase of the term so far, to 28%, while approval stands at 39%. Among Coalición Republicana voters, 81% disapprove and 4% approve. Those who backed other candidacies in 2024 show trends closer to opposition voters than to government supporters.

Opción argues this is the lowest level of support recorded by a Frente Amplio-led government at this point in a term. The measurement incorporates for the first time the controversy over the purchase of an official vehicle, which had not featured in the previous survey.

The poll was conducted by telephone in two stages, with 403 cases between July 16 and 20 and a further 403 between August 6 and 11, on a total sample of 806 people. The maximum margin of error is 3.5 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. On those parameters, the one-point change in approval is not significant, while the nine-point jump in disapproval is.

World.title: Lula's runoff lead over Flávio Bolsonaro narrows to 8.9 points, CNT/MDA poll finds
World.content:
Lula's runoff lead over Flávio Bolsonaro narrows to 8.9 points, CNT/MDA poll finds

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 09:03 UTC Full article

In the second-round scenario, Lula takes 48% of voting intentions against 39.1% for the Liberal Party senator

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva holds an 8.9-point lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff, according to the CNT/MDA poll released on Tuesday. The gap stood at 12.5 points in the June survey.

In the second-round scenario, Lula takes 48% of voting intentions against 39.1% for the Liberal Party senator. In June the figures were 49.3% and 36.8% respectively. The narrowing reflects both a 1.3-point decline for the president and a 2.3-point rise for the opposition candidate, variations that individually fall within the 2.2-point margin of error. The current gap between the two, by contrast, exceeds it comfortably. Blank and spoiled ballots account for 11% and undecided voters for 2%.

In the first round, Lula leads with 42.4%, virtually unchanged from June, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro on 28.7%, Ronaldo Caiado on 4%, Romeu Zema on 3.3% and Renan Santos on 2.8%. If no candidate exceeds 50% of valid votes, the two leading contenders go to a runoff, an outcome that has occurred in every Brazilian presidential election since 2002.

The poll tested other runoff scenarios, in which the president retains wider margins: 49% against Zema's 35%, 48% against Caiado's 36% and 49% against Renan Santos's 33%. Flávio Bolsonaro is therefore the rival who runs closest.

Measurements differ substantially depending on the polling firm. A Datafolha survey from mid-July put the runoff at 48% against 43%, four points above the figure CNT/MDA now attributes to the senator. In March, an AtlasIntel survey described the two as being in a technical tie.

The poll was commissioned by the National Transport Confederation and carried out by the MDA institute, with 2,002 face-to-face interviews conducted between August 5 and 9 in 140 municipalities across all regions of the country. The margin of error is 2.2 percentage points and the survey is registered with the Superior Electoral Court.

The figures come four days before the official start of campaigning for October's elections. Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup and endorsed his candidacy in December. Lula, 80, is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term.

World.title: Venezuela's government and opposition agree to renew the Supreme Court and claim the London gold
World.content:
Venezuela's government and opposition agree to renew the Supreme Court and claim the London gold

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 08:59 UTC Full article

National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez and Dinorah Figuera, who heads the delegated committee of the assembly elected in 2015

The government of acting president Delcy Rodríguez and a section of Venezuela's opposition closed the first round of negotiations in Caracas on Wednesday with two agreements: restarting from scratch the renewal of the Supreme Court of Justice, and acting jointly to recover Venezuelan gold reserves held at the Bank of England.

National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez and Dinorah Figuera, who heads the delegated committee of the assembly elected in 2015, signed the document and read out a joint communiqué in sections at a hotel in the capital, after more than six hours of deliberations. No questions from the press were taken.

The judicial agreement annuls the process the National Assembly had begun in May, following a reform that raised the court from 20 to 32 members. Instead, the parties agreed to amend the Supreme Court's organic law again, renew and expand the judicial nominations committee, activate a new nomination process and set up a council to review candidates' credentials. In 2024 the court upheld Nicolás Maduro's re-election despite fraud allegations and without disaggregated results being published.

On the economic front, both delegations committed to promoting the recovery of international reserve assets held at the Bank of England, some 31 tonnes of gold withheld since the United Kingdom stopped recognizing Maduro's government and the subject of litigation in London courts. Weeks ago, Delcy Rodríguez sent a letter to King Charles III requesting their release. The funds would go to assisting those affected by the June 24 double earthquake, which left more than 6,300 dead according to the official toll. The text provides for transparency, traceability and audit mechanisms over their use.

The communiqué makes no mention of the National Electoral Council, whose reform the opposition regards as a priority for any eventual election timetable, nor does it address the release of political prisoners. A group of trade unionists gathered outside the hotel calling for progress on both points. Eighty-four former political prisoners issued a statement backing the process and calling for a new court and an independent electoral authority.

Two technical working groups were set up, one on the earthquake emergency and another on strengthening democracy. Implementation begins this month and the delegations will meet again in mid-September.

This is the eighteenth attempt at negotiation in two decades, and the first held in Caracas after previous rounds in the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Doha, Oslo and Barbados. The process has the backing of the United States. María Corina Machado, in exile in Panama, remains outside the table and has said she will not obstruct it.

World.title: The main land crossing between Argentina and Chile passes its winter closure record
World.content:
The main land crossing between Argentina and Chile passes its winter closure record

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 06:55 UTC Full article

The corridor was closed as a precaution on July 14 in anticipation of the forecasts

The Cristo Redentor international crossing, which links the Argentine province of Mendoza with Chile's Valparaíso Region through the Andes, has now been closed for close to a month because of a snow and wind storm, surpassing the winter closure record set in 2023. Authorities on both sides estimate it could reopen next week, depending on weather conditions.

The corridor was closed as a precaution on July 14 in anticipation of the forecasts. Snowfall extended between the settlements of Punta de Vacas and Las Cuevas, reached accumulations of up to four meters in some sections and affected 80 kilometers of Route 7, the largest such record in the area since 2008, according to the national roads agency. Winds blew at between 110 and 160 kilometers per hour, with zero visibility.

Official counts put the number of international freight trucks held at various points in Mendoza at around 1,550, although transport sector estimates raise the figure above 2,000. Drivers from Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Chile are among those stranded. Each immobilized vehicle represents losses of close to 600 dollars a day, according to the sector's own calculations.

The delay has drawn criticism. The Mendoza truck owners' association toured the corridor and said the road was in good condition at least as far as Puente del Inca, and called for the tunnel to be opened. The national roads agency replied that clearing work reached the mouth of the international tunnel on August 9, but that winds prevent traffic being allowed through to Las Cuevas and that precautions are being intensified given the risk of avalanches.

In Chile, the head of the Border Crossings Unit, Sergio Salazar, rejected the idea that opportunities had been missed. “There really were no such windows,” he said, explaining that work on the Chilean side was completed the previous Friday and on the Argentine side this week. He said the only opening was brief and risky, and the decision was not to expose a small number of trucks.

Reopening will not restore normal traffic immediately. Authorities calculate between five and six days to clear the accumulated backlog, constrained by the winter timetable, which limits operations to around twelve hours a day. Under normal conditions the corridor handles between 500 and 600 trucks daily.

The storm has also kept the Pehuenche, Agua Negra, Pircas Negras, Pino Hachado and San Francisco crossings closed. Alternative routes to the Pacific involve travelling around 2,000 additional kilometers.

World.title: Falklands pause Loligo squid fishing for two weeks over low biomass
World.content:
Falklands pause Loligo squid fishing for two weeks over low biomass

12th Wednesday, August 2026 - 23:05 UTC Full article

The decision was taken after consultation with the industry and reflects, according to the official statement, a shared view that a temporary cessation is the most appropriate course of action

The Falkland Islands Fisheries Department announced on Wednesday that fishing within the Loligo Box will be paused for around two weeks as a precautionary measure, following low Loligo squid biomass in the area.

The decision was taken after consultation with the fishing industry and reflects, according to the official statement, a shared view that a temporary cessation is the most appropriate course of action. The Department coordinated a series of targeted trawls by the commercial fleet across the area on Wednesday, aimed at obtaining more precise information on the distribution of the stock. There were no public statements from the sector.

“This precautionary approach reflects the Department's commitment to the long-term stock sustainability and responsible management of the fishery,” the text says, adding that further updates will follow once more information is available.

Loligo squid, also known as Patagonian squid, is one of the main sources of income for the Falklands. Spain controls much of the world's catch of the species, mainly through the roughly sixteen licences the Islands grant to fish in their waters, with volumes close to 50,000 tonnes a year.

The pre-season survey carried out by the M/V Monteferro between February 3 and 18 had estimated biomass at around 41,725 tonnes, with a reliable range of between 34,726 and 60,190, a figure considered sufficient to sustain a commercial season. That survey already showed a markedly uneven distribution: 38,134 tonnes south of the Loligo Box against 3,591 tonnes in the northern zone, where around half the specimens sampled were at a very early stage of maturity.

The pause also comes after an unfavorable cycle in the archipelago's other squid fishery. The Illex season closed on June 22 with catches well below the ten-year average and against a backdrop of rising fuel costs, although the Fisheries Department and the Falkland Islands Fishing Companies Association agreed at the time that this was not an immediate cause for concern.

Squid in the southwest Atlantic is under growing pressure. Fishing effort by the Chinese fleet in the region rose 85% between 2019 and 2024, and between 300 and 500 foreign-flagged vessels operate along the outer edge of Argentina's exclusive economic zone. Argentina, which maintains a sovereignty claim over the archipelago, questions the licensing regime the Islands administer. In July, Buenos Aires enacted its accession to the FAO Port State Measures Agreement, the only binding international instrument specifically designed to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

World.title: Mexico has a trash-dumping problem. Could this new clean-up project from Monterrey be the fix?
World.content:
You see it across Mexico — on roadways, over vacant lots and along waterways. But a new project aims to create a model that could help cities tackle the nation’s illegal trash-dumping problem.

In the northern state of Nuevo León, a Tecnológico de Monterrey project is testing whether data, cleanup campaigns and community participation can turn one trash-strewn stream into a model for urban restoration.

The Arroyo Vivo initiative focuses on the 13-kilometer Arroyo Seco-San Agustín, a waterway where several sections have become illegal dumping grounds. The stream begins in the mountains above Monterrey and flows through the city before joining the La Silla River.

During 16 cleanup days since the project launched in late 2022, Tec de Monterrey researchers and volunteers have removed 21 tons of waste, finding that plastics made up more than 70% of the debris. Textiles, tires and construction rubble were also common.

The project plans to use algorithms to analyze street-level images and photographs submitted by residents, helping identify and estimate the volume of waste along the stream.

It also aims to create a biological corridor along the waterway, benefiting wildlife and nearby residents. Restoring the stream could also reduce pollution and help limit flooding risks in communities along its route during heavy rains.

Researchers are developing three-, five- and 10-year plans, while acknowledging that full ecosystem restoration could take decades.

“It’s a platform with a long-term vision,” said Nélida Escobedo, a Tec researcher. “We’re looking to consolidate a replicable intervention model that will trigger a process of ecological, social and urban regeneration in Arroyo Seco.”

The problem, of course, reaches far beyond Monterrey. Mexico City officials identified 889 illegal dumps in February, nearly half in the Cuauhtémoc, Iztapalapa and Miguel Hidalgo boroughs.

Nationally, 21% of municipal solid waste was deposited at uncontrolled sites in 2012, according to a 2015 environmental report by Semarnat, Mexico’s Environment Ministry.

The report found that 90% of metropolitan areas used sanitary landfills or controlled disposal sites, but only 4.5% of rural and semi-urban localities used sanitary landfills or controlled disposal sites.

An earlier Semarnat report, using 2011 data, put the rural and semi-urban figure at 13%.

With reports from TecScience and La Jornada

World.title: Sheinbaum, Goldman Sachs executive discuss Plan México investment at high-level meeting
World.content:
Details surrounding Mexico’s ambitious goals of becoming the world’s 10th largest economy were tabled at a Tuesday meeting between President Claudia Sheinbaum and Golden Sachs president John E. Waldron.

Plan México, the government’s flagship national economic and industrial policy, seeks to create 1.5 million new jobs, reduce imports from Asia, raise total investment to over 25% of GDP, alleviate poverty and create more specialized jobs. The plan also aims to see the Mexican economy soar from the 15th largest in the world to enter the top 10.

En Palacio Nacional, recibí al presidente y director de operaciones de Goldman Sachs, John E. Waldron, y a su equipo; conversamos sobre la percepción favorable de nuestro país en los mercados internacionales y las buenas oportunidades de inversión que brinda el Plan México. pic.twitter.com/bjszVRcLxM — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) August 12, 2026

The high-level meeting between President Sheinbaum, senior executive Waldron and Mexican finance minister Edgar Amador Zamora took place at the National Palace, in Mexico’s Historic Center. In a post on her official X account, Sheinbaum shared a photograph of the meeting and explained that they discussed the country’s “favorable perception” and the “good investment opportunities” offered by Plan México.

However, no further details regarding investments, specific projects or agreements were shared after the meeting.

Bold plan for future Mexico

Sheinbaum’s bold economic agenda was launched in January 2025 to support and protect Mexican industries amid threats to homegrown manufacturing and local industries caused by globalization.

One think tank, México ¿cómo vamos?, has questioned whether these lofty goals were on track. In a report published early this year, it found stagnant economic growth and job losses in manufacturing sectors. On a positive note, however, the think tank found improvements in the reduction of poverty for everyday Mexicans.



“Mexico can advance … [toward the achievement of] these goals if we provide greater legal certainty, openness to investment in the energy sector, and a more robust rule of law,” the MCV report concluded.

Against this backdrop, Sheinbaum’s dialogue with Goldman Sachs served as an opportunity to promote the country to one of the world’s leading investment banking firms.

Goldman Sachs first moved operations to Mexico in 1994. Since then, it has participated in debt and equity transactions, as well as mergers and acquisitions involving both private companies and public entities.

With reports from El Universal

World.title: Avocado operations fully resume in Michoacán after export pause
World.content:
U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson on Wednesday announced the full resumption of official U.S. government activities — including the processing of avocado exports — in the state of Michoacán.

In a social media post, Johnson said that security measures implemented by the Mexican government led to a positive evaluation of conditions on site, though officials will continue to monitor the situation and adjust operations as needed.

“I commend the Government of Mexico, particularly its Security Cabinet, for the actions and close coordination that made this full and efficient resumption possible,” he said. “Our priority remains the safety of U.S. personnel and the people of Michoacán.”

The U.S. — which absorbs more than 80 percent of Mexican avocado production — had suspended avocado imports from Michoacán on Aug. 5 due to unspecified “threats” to U.S. interests. It marked the third time in just over four years the avocado trade had been interrupted for security reasons, generating considerable concern among producers and packers due to the importance of the U.S. market for Michoacán’s so-called “green gold.”

In response to the suspension, the Michoacán state government deployed an additional 300 security operatives to avocado-growing regions and, the following day, the federal government ordered more than 1,500 soldiers to Michoacán.

Among the actions implemented were the installation of control points in 17 strategic packing plants and in 29 producing municipalities, while a new intelligence center was established in the city of Uruapan, often referred to as the avocado capital of the world.

Two days later, the suspension was partially lifted.

Johnson said the outcome of the past week’s developments demonstrates that the security and prosperity of the two neighboring nations can be strengthened by effective cooperation.

Working together, he said, protects the public, food production, supply chains and legitimate trade. He called it “a tangible result of the cooperation advanced by President Trump and President Sheinbaum.”

In contrast, the U.S. Embassy also reiterated its official travel advisory for Michoacán, which designates the state a “Level 4 – Do Not Travel” area.

The Embassy reminded U.S. citizens of some measures they should take if traveling to the western state.

Monitor local media for updates

Keep family and friends informed of your location and well-being via phone, text and social media

Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP)

Call 911 in case of emergency

Contact the U.S. Embassy if you need assistance

With reports from El Universal, Informador and Meganoticias

World.title: Oaxaca was the right choice for my one big Mexico trip. A review by MND’s summer intern
World.content:
I was considering a lot of places for my one big trip while in Mexico.

Six weeks ago, I arrived in San Miguel de Allende to start a nine-week journalism internship with Mexico News Daily. I had already travelled to Mexico City, Querétaro and Guanajuato. But there was still so much I had not seen and so many places I wanted to explore.

I could have gone to one of Mexico’s iconic coastal cities. I could have gone to the Sierra Gorda or visited the caves at Tolantongo, but I landed on Oaxaca.

The southern Mexican city is world-famous for its historic colonial center, ancient ruins, local cuisine and landscape. It had everything I was looking for in a weekend excursion — and a new direct flight from Querétaro made the trip seamless.

But once I landed I immediately started to wonder if the city would live up to my lofty expectations, especially after Travel + Leisure magazine rated it the fifth best city in the world. Would the weather cooperate? Would I be impressed with the colonial center after living in San Miguel de Allende? Would Monte Albán — a massive archaeological site adorned with Zapotec pyramids — be too crowded to enjoy?

The most apparent thing when I stepped out of Oaxaca’s minuscule international airport was that it was very different from other cities I had visited in Mexico. It has not adapted for the comfort of international tourists with luxury hotels or pristine streets. It is rugged and sometimes dirty. There is more of an emphasis on adventure than in places like Cancún or San Miguel de Allende, which offer more relaxing vacations.

Oaxaca is also the third-poorest state in Mexico, with over half of the population living on less than US $62 per month, according to the Borgen Project. Dilapidated infrastructure is commonplace, the poverty of some towns is eye-opening and the social exclusion experienced in the state is evident — not a comfortable experience for a lot of tourists.

But my experience still lived up to my expectations, and sometimes even blew them out of the water.

After spending almost two months living in San Miguel and taking a trip to Guanajuato, I did not find Oaxaca’s colonial city center to be particularly impressive. However, it is still full of colorful streets and ornate architecture where massive Catholic churches dominate the skyline. The most impressive church — the Temple of Santo Domingo de Guzmán — features the Museum of Oaxacan Cultures, which is filled with artifacts thousands of years old and features incredible views of the surrounding gardens and mountains.

But the real adventure came the day after I arrived when I boarded a van headed for Hierve el Agua, an incredible rock formation about 90 minutes east of the city with natural hot springs and otherworldly calcified waterfalls. The tour also stopped at ancient ruins as well as mezcal and textile factories. It was a long 12-hour tour, but the unbelievable views and immersion into Oaxaca’s unique culture were well worth it.

That is the intrigue of Oaxaca: its Indigenous roots are on display everywhere throughout the city, from the street art throughout Centro to the alebrijes lining the artisan shops to the unique food and dress. And just beyond, you’ll find wondrous access to nature. Oaxaca is also one of the few places in Mexico where residents openly speak Zapotec and Mixtec in addition to Spanish. It is an experience that truly cannot be replicated because it is unique to Oaxaca itself.

And the history is some of the oldest in the world. Oaxaca — along with most of southern Mexico — is considered one of six cradles of civilization in the world, where farming was developed independently. The Zapotec people have lived in Oaxaca for thousands of years — with some Monte Alban pyramids dating back 2,500 years.

So did Oaxaca live up to the expectations? Absolutely.

World.title: Why was Mexico’s military rescue brigade barred from entering Colombia? Thursday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🇨🇴 Mexican rescue brigade denied entry to Colombia: Sheinbaum clarified that, contrary to what she said Wednesday, the Mexican Army’s rescue brigade has not actually traveled to Colombia to assist the earthquake response, as the new government of President de la Espriella requested a certification it does not have. It remains ready to deploy.

Sheinbaum clarified that, contrary to what she said Wednesday, the Mexican Army’s rescue brigade has not actually traveled to Colombia to assist the earthquake response, as the new government of President de la Espriella requested a certification it does not have. It remains ready to deploy. 📦 Aid still flowing: Despite the rescue brigade holdup, Mexico is sending 58.5 tonnes of humanitarian aid to Colombia via Air Force flights this week.

Despite the rescue brigade holdup, Mexico is sending 58.5 tonnes of humanitarian aid to Colombia via Air Force flights this week. 📰 Sheinbaum rejects PAN’s “right of reply” bill: Asked about opposition legislation seeking airtime to respond to statements made at the mañanera, Sheinbaum said the conference is “the people’s space” and that political parties should create their own spaces.

Asked about opposition legislation seeking airtime to respond to statements made at the mañanera, Sheinbaum said the conference is “the people’s space” and that political parties should create their own spaces. 📱 SIM card registration deadline looms: Saturday, Aug. 15 is the deadline for prepaid phone numbers ending in 0 to be linked to a verified identity. Sheinbaum said linking SIM cards to identities will help authorities investigate phone-based extortion.

Why today’s mañanera matters

At her Thursday morning press conference, President Claudia Sheinbaum revealed that the government of Colombia had not approved the entry of Mexican military personnel to assist the response to the earthquake on Monday that toppled buildings in various cities and towns in the South American country.

Reuters reported on Thursday morning that the death toll from the quake had risen to 265, according to the latest figures released by President Abelardo de la Espriella. “Authorities also reported 3,494 injured and 496 missing, as emergency teams continue searching for survivors in the rubble,” the news agency wrote.

Had the earthquake occurred during the presidency of Gustavo Petro, whose four-year term ended last week, rescue personnel from the Mexican military would likely have entered Colombia without any problem. Sheinbaum and Petro developed a close working relationship and are of the same political persuasion. In contrast, the new Colombian president was recently described by France 24 as a “far-right Trump fan.”

Also of note at today’s mañanera was Sheinbaum’s response to a “right of reply” bill presented by the National Action Party (PAN).

El Heraldo de México reported on Wednesday that the bill aims to “regulate” Sheinbaum’s mañaneras via the issuance of a new law called the Social Communication Law for the Federal Executive Power. The draft law, El Heraldo reported, seeks to “guarantee the right of reply” for citizens who are “slandered” during the president’s weekday press conferences.

Mexican military personnel denied entry to Colombia

At the start of her press conference, Sheinbaum noted that she said on Wednesday that a brigade of Mexican Army rescuers had traveled to Colombia to assist the response to the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck the South American country on Monday.

She clarified that the brigade had not in fact traveled to Colombia.

“They asked for certification,” Sheinbaum said, referring to the government of Colombia, led since last Friday by President de la Espriella.

She said that the Mexican Army rescue brigade “is certified” but the Colombian government is asking for “another certification.”

“… To clarify, the rescue brigade of the National Defense Ministry was not approved by the government of Colombia. It is ready to leave at any time,” Sheinbaum said.

She reiterated that Mexico is sending humanitarian aid to Colombia. Sheinbaum said on Wednesday that the Mexican Air Force would deliver a total of 58.5 tonnes of Mexican aid, including food, medicine and other essential goods, to the South American country this week.

Sheinbaum: Political parties ‘should create their own information space’

A reporter asked the president about the “right of reply” bill put forward by the PAN, Mexico’s main opposition party.

“What they argue in their bill is [that they should] have the same space, with the same dissemination as the mañanera,” the reporter said.

“… They want their right of reply [to statements made at the mañanera] in a space with the same ratings. Will the president’s office be open to this?” she asked.

Sheinbaum responded that “everyone has their own space.”

“This is a space for the people,” she said.

“It’s the mañanera of the people. It’s a space where the government of Mexico exercises the responsibility to inform the people,” Sheinbaum said.

“If people watch us it’s because they like the mañanera,” she said. “If they didn’t like it, they wouldn’t watch us.”

Sheinbaum noted that the mañanera — transmitted every weekday from 7:30 a.m. — is one of the most watched live programs on social media.

“This has to do with the way in which we inform … [and] that the people are attentive,” she said.

“A political party can do it as well. They have their right to do so, but each in their own space,” Sheinbaum said.

“… This is the space for the mañanera of the people. If the PAN, the PRI or even Morena wants to have their own space, they should create their own information space,” she said.

“If they don’t have [good] ratings, well, what are we going to do?”

The first deadline to register pre-paid cell phones is this Saturday

A reporter asked the president whether cell phone lines would be cut off this Saturday, as Aug. 15 is the deadline for people with pre-paid numbers ending in 0 to link their personal identity to their number. Pre-paid cell phone users can do so by completing a registration process with their telephone companies.

The reporter said that some 8 million people haven’t yet registered their pre-paid cell phones.

Sheinbaum said that anyone whose telephone service is cut can “recover their line simply by registering.”

“Why was this done? … One of the problems we have in some entities of the republic is extortion. … A lot of these threats are made by telephone,” she said.

Sheinbaum said that having pre-paid phones linked to people’s identity will assist authorities in their investigations into telephone extortion.

“… We’re one of the few countries in the world, maybe the only one, where a SIM card is not linked to a person. So what is being asked? That when you buy a SIM card … you provide your identity in order to take care of each other,” she said.

World.title: June tourist numbers fall short of World Cup expectations
World.content:
The tourism boom Mexican authorities anticipated from co-hosting the FIFA men’s World Cup didn’t materialize, official data shows.

The national statistics agency INEGI reported on Thursday that 4.11 million international tourists came to Mexico in June, an increase of just 1.1% compared to the same month of last year. The term “international tourists” refers to visitors who spend at least one night in the country.

En junio 2026, ingresaron al país 8,189,014 viajeras y viajeros internacionales, 2.1% más que en junio 2025. De esta cantidad:

▪️50.2% entraron como turistas internacionales (residentes en el extranjero que se hospedaron al menos una noche en México)

▪️49.8% lo hicieron como… pic.twitter.com/UyPkARgn73 — INEGI INFORMA (@INEGI_INFORMA) August 13, 2026

The year-over-year growth in international tourists was the lowest of any month so far this year, even though Mexico hosted 12 of its 13 World Cup games in June. (The 13th game was July 5.)

Mexican authorities had anticipated that the World Cup would bring up to to 5.5 million additional tourists to Mexico, but that prediction proved to be overly optimistic.

INEGI’s data shows that the number of international tourists who arrived in Mexico by air in June fell 5.3% annually to 1.75 million. Therefore, only 42.6% of the international tourists who came to Mexico in June flew into the country. The remaining 57.4% of international tourists entered the country by land from the United States, Guatemala or Belize.

International traveler numbers increased 2.1% in June, spending rose 5.9%

INEGI reported that just under 8.19 million international travelers came to Mexico in June, an increase of 2.1% compared to the same month of last year. The term “international travelers” refers to both international tourists and international day-trippers.

In June, 4.07 million international day-trippers — including cruise ship visitors — came to Mexico, a 3.2% annual increase. That figure represents 49.8% of the total number of international travelers to Mexico last month. The remaining 50.2% were international tourists.

The most positive takeaway from INEGI’s latest tourism data is that international travelers’ spending in Mexico increased 5.9% annually to US $2.91 billion in June. In May, expenditure declined 0.3% annually.

Spending by international tourists increased 6.3% annually to $2.65 billion in June, representing 91.1% of the total. Spending by international day-trippers increased 1.5% annually to $259 million.

The average expenditure in Mexico of international tourists in June was $645.20 per person, an annual increase of 5.2%. Among international tourists who arrived by air, the outlay per person was almost double at $1,283.80, an annual increase of 9.6%.

International day-trippers spent an average of just $63.50 per person during their visits in June, an annual decrease of 1.7%. Within that category, spending in Mexico by cruise ship passengers was higher at $87 per person, a 7% annual increase.

At President Claudia Sheinbaum’s Thursday morning press conference, Tourism Minister Josefina Rodríguez said that spending by international travelers in June was the highest this year.

While the overall growth in tourists was modest, she highlighted that visitors from some countries increased significantly in annual terms in June, including Japan (+131.7%); Australia (+89.1%); Colombia (+74.4%); Ecuador (+62.6%); and South Korea (+46.7%).

The national soccer teams from four of those five countries played World Cup matches in Mexico in June. Australia was the only team that didn’t play a match in the country.

The US was the top source of international ‘non-border’ tourists

INEGI published data that showed that 2.2 million of the 4.11 million international tourists who came to Mexico in June were “non-border tourists” — i.e. they spent at least one night in parts of the country not located near Mexico’s northern or southern borders.

Of those 2.2 million people, almost 1.53 million people, or 69.2% of the total, live in the United States.

INEGI also reported that in June:

303,721 non-border international tourists came from South American and Caribbean countries. That figure represents 13.8% of the total.

124,709 non-border international tourists came from Canada (5.7% of the total).

99,180 non-border international tourists came from Central American countries (4.5% of the total).

77,875 non-border international tourists came from European countries (3.5% of the total).

43,400 non-border international tourists came from Asian countries (2% of the total).

31,002 non-border international tourists came from “other regions” of the world (1.4% of the total).

Tourism minister presents record January-June tourism data

At Sheinbaum’s Thursday press conference, Rodríguez also reported that a record high 51.1 million international travelers came to Mexico in the first six months of 2026, an annual increase of 7.7%.

She said that international tourist numbers also reached a record high at 24.5 million between January and June. That figure represents a 4.6% year-over-year increase.

Rodríguez reported that spending by international travelers increased 0.5% annually in the first six months of the year to reach a record high $18.78 billion.

Although the increase in spending was minimal, the tourism minister stressed that expenditure didn’t decline “despite the inflation affecting the United States and the increase in the cost of flights, especially long-distance ones.”

Rodríguez also reported that a record high 6.6 million cruise ship passengers visited Mexico in the first six months of the year, an annual increase of 15.2%. She said that “spending by cruise ship passengers, which is what we’re looking for,” was a record $575 million between January and June, an annual increase of 18.7%.

Rodríguez highlights increase in domestic tourism

Rodríguez also reported that 53.6 million Mexicans spent at least one night in a hotel in Mexico in the first six months of the year. She said that figure represented an increase of 733,000 people compared to the same period of last year.

Rodríguez stressed the importance of domestic tourism to Mexican destinations.

“Not all destinations are filled with foreign tourists. Rather, a lot of them, 80% of them, depend on us,” she said.

With reports from EFE and El Sol de México

World.title: How a Tijuana ceramicist turned desert animals into an interior design concept
World.content:
When Sócrates Medina first started playing around with ceramics, he found it served a therapeutic purpose, helping to channel and manage the ADHD he’d been struggling with. However, he could never have imagined it would become a successful studio with international collaborators across various disciplines.

Medina founded Perro Y Arena, an aesthetic ceramics design studio, in 2018 while living in Los Angeles. Initially, the work was nothing more than a passion project. However, in 2021, the artist moved back to his native Tijuana, a border town roughly 140 miles south of L.A. in the Mexican state of Baja California, to turn his nascent hobby into a full-fledged career.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by perro y arena® 〰️ (@perroyarena)

Since then, Medina’s creative universe has expanded through collaborations with artists, designers, other ceramic artisans and textile creators. The studio hosts pop-up events in cities such as Los Angeles, San Diego, Tijuana and Mexico City.

From desert mythology to the world

Medina’s early ceramic sculptures were inspired by the profound connection between humans and dogs in Mexican culture, such as the once-nearly extinct hairless Colima dog, which Mesoamerican societies revered as a guardian in both the mortal and metaphysical planes.

The creatures Medina looked to largely came from the desert landscapes he calls home. The coyote, for example, has “symbolic significance in Tijuana as a symbol of the border,” Medina says, adding, “I really identify with this animal.”

Over time, his animals have grown more fantastical, borrowing elements not only from Mexican mythology, but also Greek and Egyptian art, while still maintaining an aesthetic defined by minimalist lines that echo desert landscapes as well as symbols from nahualism, or Indigenous shamanic traditions.

The desert as a muse

For Medina, the desert is a natural source of inspiration.

“When I started focusing on a desert-like aesthetic with a Mediterranean, sandy palette and pale, warm colours, that’s when I began devoting myself 100% to the project,” he says.

He’s experimented with other colors, such as yellow and blue, but always juxtaposed with his signature sand tone.

Thematically, every piece evokes the desert’s mysticism. According to Perro Y Arena, the animal figurines invite the viewer “into a spiritual and mythological world where you can dance with coyotes and hares while serenading the moon.”

Living vicariously through his art



Medina’s connection to his craft goes beyond the art of creation. Rather, his pieces serve as something of an alter ego; each sculpture a vessel for personal reflection and quiet introspection.

He explained that when he first started creating his dogs, they represented states of being or attributes he desired for himself. He also feels a deep bond with them, viewing them as a living synthesis of rural and urban creatures.

But his ceramic designs also serve as a philosophical statement, often depicted engaged in meditative activities.

“It’s as if my characters do or become things that I want for myself. I want to be calm, to reflect and to enjoy a cup of coffee,” Medina says. “Sometimes I give them a tattoo or an earring that I’d like to have myself. They’re like a fantasy version of me, an alter ego.”

Perro y Arena invites us to pause and enjoy the moment. “One of my favorite pieces is an incense holder,” Medina says. “The simple act of lighting and arranging incense is a reminder to make time for ourselves.”

Crows, rabbits, serpents, coyotes and dogs are all part of this unique, handmade collection, which captures a dynamic aesthetic with nothing more than a few lines.

Ana Paula de la Torre is a Mexican journalist and collaborator for various outlets, including Milenio, Animal Político, Vice, Newsweek en Español, Televisa and Mexico News Daily.

World.title: Mexico in Numbers: How do Mexicans spend their time?
World.content:
Every five years, the national statistics agency INEGI conducts a National Survey on Time Use (ENUT).

The most recent survey was conducted at more than 32,000 homes in 2024. The results of the survey were published in August 2025.

In this week’s “Mexico in Numbers” article, we look at some of the key results.

Reading about how Mexicans spend their days and weeks may seem uninteresting on the surface. But some of the ENUT results might just surprise you! And, after all, how we spend our time is how we live our lives.

* N.B. — Males and females aged 12 and over participated in the 2024 ENUT.

How many hours do Mexicans work per week?

On average, Mexicans spend 59.6 hours per week performing paid and unpaid work, including domestic chores, care work and volunteer work.

In other words, Mexicans spend around 35% of their time each week working.

On average, women work 61.1 hours per week while men work 58 hours per week.

On average, women spend 39.7 hours per week on domestic chores, care work and volunteer work, compared to 18.2 hours for men. Thus, the weekly gender gap for such work is 21.5 hours.

In households where the occupants speak an Indigenous language, the weekly gender gap for domestic, care and volunteer work is even higher at 27.3 hours. For Mexicans who live in towns with fewer than 10,000 residents, the weekly gender gap for domestic, care and volunteer work is also much higher than the national average at 26.4 hours.

The state where people, on average, spend the most hours per week working is Hidalgo. On average, hidalguenses work 65.6 hours per week, six hours more than the national average.

The state where people, on average, spend the fewest hours per week working is Chihuahua. On average, chihauhuenses work 54.5 hours per week, 5.1 hours less than the national average.

How many hours do Mexicans sleep per week?

According to the results of the 2024 ENUT, women in Mexico, on average, sleep 53 hours per week. In other words, women usually get just over 7 1/2 hours of sleep per night.

On average, men sleep 52.1 hours per week, or just under 7 1/2 hours per night.

On average, women in Mexico spend 114.1 hours per week working and sleeping. Thus, women are left with 53.9 hours per week for other activities.

On average, men in Mexico spend 110.1 hours per week working and sleeping. Consequently, men are left with 57.9 hours per week for other activities.

How do Mexicans spend their time when they’re not working or sleeping?

In addition to working and sleeping, Mexicans — like people around the world — spend time eating, bathing, attending to their personal health needs and resting.

According to the 2024 ENUT results, women, on average, spend 8.6 hours per week eating while men spend 8.2 hours per week chowing down (on tasty Mexican food in many cases, no doubt).

On average, women spend 6.7 hours per week on bathing, dressing and personal grooming; 5.4 hours on their personal healthcare needs; and 4.1 hours praying, meditating and resting.

On average, men spend 5.6 hours per week on bathing, dressing and personal grooming; 6.1 hours on their personal health care needs; and 4.6 hours praying, meditating and resting.

The most popular “free time” activity for both women and men is “use of mass media” — e.g., surfing the internet; posting to social media or sending online messages; watching TV, movies and streaming services; listening to music and the radio; and reading material such as books, newspapers and magazines.

On average, women spend 15.1 hours per week using mass media, while men spend 15.7 hours per week on the same activity.

The next most popular “free time” activity for Mexicans is spending time with friends and family. The average time spent on such convivencia (coexistence) per week is 7.8 hours for women and 7 hours for men.

The third most popular “free time” activity for women is sports and physical exercise, with an average of 4.7 hours per week spent on such activities. On average, men spend 5.4 hours playing sports and doing exercise per week. However, sports and exercise only rank as the fourth most popular “free time” activity for men.

Mexican men’s third most popular leisure activity is “participation in games and hobbies.” On average, men spend 6.1 hours per week playing games and practicing their hobbies. The average for women is 4.1 hours, making games and hobbies the fourth most popular pastime for mexicanas.

So, how do you spend the 168 hours at your disposal each week? In what ways does your life differ from that of the average Mexican? Let us know in the comments.

World.title: Petz Cobasi Q2 2026 Profit Rises 8.4% to R$70 Million
World.content:
Brazil · Retail

Key Facts The result Petz Cobasi’s adjusted profit rose to R$70.3 million (about US$13.6 million) in the second quarter of 2026.

Petz Cobasi’s adjusted profit rose to R$70.3 million (about US$13.6 million) in the second quarter of 2026. The growth That is up 8.4% from a year earlier — real growth, with pet prices barely rising.

That is up 8.4% from a year earlier — real growth, with pet prices barely rising. The headline number Reported profit jumped 43.5% to R$100.4 million (about US$19.5 million), lifted by one-off tax credits.

Reported profit jumped 43.5% to R$100.4 million (about US$19.5 million), lifted by one-off tax credits. The merger This is Brazil’s combined pet giant, born from the Petz and Cobasi tie-up.

This is Brazil’s combined pet giant, born from the Petz and Cobasi tie-up. Sales Net revenue rose 7.9% to R$1.7 billion (about US$329 million); same-store sales grew 7.1%.

Net revenue rose 7.9% to R$1.7 billion (about US$329 million); same-store sales grew 7.1%. Online Digital sales reached R$855.6 million (about US$166 million), now 40.6% of the total.

Brazilians keep spending on their dogs and cats even when money is tight. The country’s newly merged pet-store champion is turning that loyalty into steady profit.

Here is the Petz Cobasi Q2 2026 profit you should know about: Brazil’s largest pet-care retailer, formed by merging the Petz and Cobasi chains, grew its adjusted profit to R$70.3 million (about US$13.6 million) from April to June — solid growth in a quarter when prices barely moved.

A Petz store in Brazil. The merged Petz Cobasi group posted higher second-quarter profit. (Photo: Internet Reproduction)
